didnt: Rejected — a full ML data-labelling platform whose scale, commercial edition split and training-data focus far exceed our approval-gated wiki annotation need; nothing in it fills a gap in our stack. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: INCEpTION
good: A semantic annotation platform offering multi-layer annotation (entities, relations, coreference, syntax, frames, document labels) against your own ontology — loading RDF, OWL, OBO, SKOS or Turtle, or querying a live SPARQL endpoint such as Wikidata. Recommenders learn from accepted annotations and apply active learning, and nothing is stored until the annotator accepts a suggestion; it adds curation into a gold standard with inter-annotator agreement measurement, a REST API and webhooks, PDF/HTML/TEI import and UIMA CAS/CoNLL-U export, runs as a desktop installer or an institutional server with SSO, and is actively maintained (21,899 commits, 279 releases) under Apache-2.0.
bad: It is a heavy Java/UIMA platform with a substantial learning and administration surface — separate user, admin and developer guides plus tutorial videos — designed for corpus-building teams, and its native formats are NLP-corpus artefacts (CAS XMI, CoNLL-U), which is far more machinery than a personal wiki needs.
didnt: Board — its rule that recommender suggestions are stored only when a human accepts them, combined with ontology/SPARQL entity linking and agreement-checked curation, as a model for suggestion-then-approve annotation over wiki pages; the Java/UIMA platform itself is too heavy to adopt. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)
institution: TU Darmstadt (UKP Lab)

name: WebAnno
good: A general-purpose web-based annotation tool for morphological, syntactic and semantic linguistic annotation, with custom layers for non-linguistic tasks, multi-user roles (annotator, curator, project manager), and monitoring of project progress and quality through inter-annotator agreement. It offers correction and automation modes and needs nothing but a browser for annotators once installed on a server; Apache-2.0 licensed.
bad: The project's own site steers users away from it — a banner urges 'You like WebAnno? Use INCEpTION!', presenting INCEpTION as the successor with more features, and notes that WebAnno automation/correction projects cannot be imported into it. Its focus remains linguistic corpus annotation rather than general knowledge work.
didnt: Corroboration — role-separated annotation (annotator/curator/project manager) with agreement-based quality monitoring confirms our gated, curated write model; no separate adoption, since the project itself directs new users to INCEpTION as its successor. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)
institution: TU Darmstadt (UKP Lab)

name: whichmen/dxl-commerce-agent
good: A complete OpenClaw + LLM e-commerce customer-service system covering Taobao, Pinduoduo, Douyin, Kuaishou, Xiaohongshu and WeChat Channels: the model must fetch business facts through 13 permission-gated tools (orders, logistics, refunds, identity) rather than answering from memory, write and high-risk tools are off by default with backend validation, and it ships send receipts, idempotency keys, per-session serial processing, manual takeover, watchdog recovery, 72 automated tests and 50 deterministic offline evals with a secret scan in CI.
bad: A brand-new single-author project (created 2026-08-13, 15 commits, no releases). It is bound to Chinese platform UIs through browser/Appium automation, and the README admits page-structure upgrades may require selector changes; the Docker Compose path only exercises the fixed-rule policy fallback, not the real model chain, and customer messages and receipts accumulate in SQLite under the operator's own retention duty.
didnt: Rejected — an e-commerce customer-service system for Chinese marketplaces, outside the knowledge-wiki scope; its read-only-by-default tool gating corroborates our approval design but there is nothing here to adopt. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Chandler-Sun/MemChinesePalace
licence: MIT (per README License section; no LICENSE file in repo root)
good: A memory-palace system (palace/wing/room) storing each memory twice — a compressed 'bamboo slip' in Wenjian, a Classical Chinese shorthand spec with type headers and status marks, alongside the full original 'wooden tablet' that is never lost — with a four-layer memory stack (about 170 tokens of always-loaded wakeup context), a temporal SQLite knowledge graph with contradiction detection and fact invalidation, and 20 MCP tools; fully local with no API key required.
bad: The author states in the repo description itself that it is 'not a serious project'; it has 8 commits. Its compression and retrieval figures (e.g. 94.8% R@10 with palace filtering, 28% fewer tokens than AAAK) are self-reported single examples, and the deliberately lossy classical-Chinese shorthand depends on the model interpreting terse text correctly; the palace architecture is openly derived from MemPalace.
didnt: Board — the compressed-slip-plus-full-original pairing, typed memory headers with status marks, and the tiny always-loaded wakeup layer are board-worthy memory-design ideas; the project itself is a self-described experiment. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: wink-wink-wink555/WordNest
good: A personalised English-vocabulary system built on Flask: it only collects words the user adds themselves (no bulk word lists), generates example sentences and mnemonics locally with Ollama + Qwen, draws a DeepSeek-powered vocabulary knowledge graph, and runs fully locally/offline with CSV export, random self-testing and star marking of hard words.
bad: A single-user Flask hobby app; its knowledge-graph feature is labelled Beta and requires a DeepSeek cloud API key, and no spaced-repetition algorithm is described — review is random draws, hiding definitions, and manual starring.
didnt: Rejected — a personal vocabulary-learning app, not knowledge infrastructure; nothing our wiki needs from it. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: jaychouya/MemoryAgent
good: A local memory sidecar for any agent: four memory types (user profile, behavioural feedback, project state, external references) stored as human-readable Markdown + YAML files that can be edited in Obsidian, hybrid FTS + persistent-vector recall with reranking and visible Memory Citations (score, type, staleness hint), an L0 evidence chain tracing atomic memories back to the source conversation fragments, defaults that filter out chit-chat and code-derivable facts, a golden-set Recall@5 evaluation with a CI gate, and MCP v2, HTTP API and standalone-chat access with 15+ LLM providers.
bad: A very young (created 2026-06-01) single-author project. It is deliberately only a memory layer — no knowledge authoring or search product — and parts of its storage story are aspirational: the README's architecture note says the Redis/PostgreSQL implementations under src/memory/layers exist only for tests and future extension while the runtime path is local files plus SQLite.
didnt: Corroboration — its Markdown memory files with citation display, staleness hints and L0 provenance confirm our own memory design choices; a separate sidecar is unnecessary because our wiki already plays this role. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: alg-bug-engineer/Cheesy-AI-Fish
licence: no licence stated at source (no LICENSE file and no licence statement in the README)
good: A large, sustained personal knowledge corpus: roughly 300 technical articles (about 1.2 million characters) on LLMs, RAG, agents and prompt engineering, kept as plain Markdown with images and code in an Obsidian vault organised by month and topic — evidence of the personal-wiki practice itself.
bad: It is a personal notes dump, not a system: no software, no retrieval or Q&A layer, and no licence anywhere in the repo, so nothing in it is licensed for reuse; the root even carries a stray v1.py and .DS_Store.
didnt: Rejected — a personal notes archive, not a tool; there is nothing to adopt, and no licence covers reuse of its content. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: ikevss/wechat-ai-memory
good: A local-first Windows tool that turns WeChat chats into a personal memory library: it reads Windows WeChat 4.x read-only (decrypting a temporary copy, never writing database keys to disk, no telemetry or uploads), filters by conversation, date range and keyword, restores original images, transcribes SILK voice messages locally with faster-whisper, and exports traceable PDF, Markdown and structured-JSON context packs an agent can read and cite.
bad: Alpha software (v0.3.6-alpha, private testing): Windows-only and bound to WeChat 4.x internals that can break on any WeChat upgrade; binaries are unsigned and its Frida process reading can trip security software; AI Q&A, RAG and OCR are explicitly not yet implemented — full-text search, a persistent memory store and MCP are roadmap items only.
didnt: Rejected — a single-platform chat exporter at alpha stage; our ingest already covers the sources we control, and WeChat is not among them. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: NiuXiangQian/chatgpt-stream
good: A deliberately minimal Java/Spring Boot integration for OpenAI: SSE streaming responses with no third-party dependencies, in-session chat memory, image generation, Markdown rendering with code highlighting, an API key list used in round-robin, and a CompletedCallBack hook so a host business system can persist questions and answers itself.
bad: A 2023-era demo pinned to gpt-3.5-turbo / gpt-4; its 'chat memory' is only in-conversation context, not a memory system, there is no retrieval and no persistence layer of its own, and the author concedes the frontend styling is rough.
didnt: Rejected — a streaming chat demo, not knowledge or memory infrastructure. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: moyangzhan/langchain4j-aideepin-web
good: The web frontend of the langchain4j-aideepin AI productivity platform (chat, drawing, knowledge base / RAG, workflows, an MCP service marketplace, speech input/output and long-term memory), a Vue/TypeScript app with Docker support and a long release history (39 releases) before the merge.
bad: The standalone repository is dead: its README is only a notice that the code was merged into the langchain4j-aideepin monorepo as user-web/, and as a frontend alone it carries none of the platform's knowledge-base or memory logic, which lives in the backend elsewhere.
didnt: Rejected — an archived frontend shell superseded by its monorepo; there is nothing to take from this repository itself. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: LiangNiang/OpenMantis
good: A lightweight single-user agent chat framework (Bun + Vercel AI SDK) connecting multiple LLM providers to Feishu, WeCom and QQ with composable tool groups, a scheduler and browser automation. Its memory system is genuinely specified: four cognitive memory types (semantic / procedural / episodic / prospective), each memory a frontmatter Markdown file indexed by a single MEMORY.md that is always injected into the system prompt, with a soft warning at 400 lines, a hard cap of 500 lines that refuses writes and rolls back, LLM-driven conflict detection before saving, and idle sessions auto-archived into structured recaps (goal / decisions / changes / todos).
bad: The repository is archived on GitHub. It is explicitly single-user — the README states it has no multi-tenancy, user isolation or permission management — its memory retrieval is index injection plus on-demand file reads with no semantic search, and its own roadmap already calls for a memory-system redesign.
didnt: Board — the typed memory files with per-type required structure, the hard-capped always-loaded index with write rollback, and the idle-session structured recap are directly board-worthy for our memory design, even though the repository itself is archived. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: xvirobotics/metabot
good: Self-hosted infrastructure for supervised, self-improving agent organisations: run Codex, Kimi Code or Claude Code from Feishu, Telegram, Slack, WeChat or Web, with multiple bots holding separate engines, workspaces and sessions yet cooperating through Agent Teams and an Agent Bus that supports stable sessions and idempotency-keyed safe retries; MetaMemory gives cross-session knowledge retrieval syncable to a Feishu knowledge base, T5T keeps persistent project checkpoints and goals, and the installer verifies checksums/signatures and stores its token at 0600 without logging it.
bad: A young, fast-moving project (created 2026-02-07) whose current open-source state is partial by its own account — Codex app-server support and in-flight steering are still to come. Its agents can read, write and execute code in configured workspaces, and the README's security section pushes safety onto token and channel hygiene; one shared token gates the whole console (chat, memory, teams, CLI access).
didnt: Corroboration — supervised multi-agent orchestration with persistent checkpoints, idempotent bus messaging and shared memory mirrors our own multi-agent arrangement; nothing was adopted directly. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: qiqihezh/deepresearch-agent
licence: MIT (per README License section; no LICENSE file in repo root)
good: A from-scratch deep-research agent system: a self-built asyncio DAG orchestrator with a 9-state state machine and three-level degradation/replanning, a Red-Blue adversarial denoising loop (a Red agent attacks reports on factuality, logic, citation quality, coverage and timeliness; a Blue agent repairs via ADD/DELETE/MODIFY/VERIFY, with score, delta and round-cap termination plus oscillation detection), three-level semantic context compression (embedding filter, TextRank key-sentence extraction, verbatim retention for the most relevant), a cross-agent shared memory store with write-time dedupe and three contradiction-resolution strategies, per-module model routing, and a serious evaluation suite (165 experiment runs, a 35-question ResearchBench, bootstrap confidence intervals and Cohen's d).
bad: The repository has 4 commits and no releases — the whole system landed at once. Its roadmap admits experiment results are still being filled in, so the headline evaluation claims are not yet backed by published results; the GRPO evolution engine is a reserved interface rather than working code; and running it needs several paid API keys (DeepSeek, Bocha search).
didnt: Board — the Red-Blue adversarial review loop with convergence and oscillation detection is a board-worthy pattern for report quality assurance; the repository itself is too fresh and unverified to adopt. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Sallyn0225/eidolon-sc
good: A fan-made AI companion for Idolmaster Shiny Colors idols with real-time WebRTC voice chat (Japanese voice with Chinese subtitles, interruptible), characters who recall only story events they actually appeared in, cross-character shared memory voiced with attribution ('I heard it from Hiori...') that users can inspect and delete, per-user memory isolation on a public deployment, bring-your-own-keys stored only in the browser, need-based retrieval gating so chit-chat pays no retrieval latency, full data-pack export/import, and architecture decisions documented as ADRs.
bad: An unofficial fan work built on copyrighted characters and story data that is deliberately not distributed — users must source the story corpus themselves, and an ADR acknowledges the risk that characters indirectly disclose story content to logged-in users. It is AGPL-licensed, and its memory serves roleplay continuity, not knowledge work.
didnt: Rejected — a fandom voice companion; its shared-memory-with-attribution is charming but belongs to roleplay, and AGPL plus third-party IP rule out any reuse. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: xuanlinAI/overmind
good: An ambitious 'cognitive engine' add-on for Claude Code: a five-layer memory system (SQLite + FTS5 semantic memory, procedural memories auto-promoted after three repeats of a pattern, episodic session summaries, a 10-relation knowledge graph with BFS causal chains), 20 MCP tools, a fleet mode in which multiple Claude Code instances discover each other through a local daemon and share broadcasts and conflict detection, gated pipeline stages (commit gate, red-team review, budget stop-loss), and an adaptive installer that snapshots before installing and rolls back if its smoke test fails.
bad: Its extraordinary claims (0.001ms p50 core latency, 'the first cognitive nervous system', 4,500+ graph nodes) rest on the project's own self-test checklist rather than independent verification; 66 flat JavaScript modules in the repo root with names like quantum.js, dream.js and theory_of_mind.js signal concept sprawl over depth; there are no releases, and parts of the system require a DeepSeek API key.
didnt: Rejected — unverifiable self-reported metrics and a sprawling single-author design; its fleet-broadcast idea echoes our own filings pattern, but nothing here is solid enough to board. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: alingalingling/Astrbot-wechat-bot-
licence: MIT (per README licence section; no LICENSE file in repo root)
good: A small bridge that turns a WeChat alt account into an AI bot: wxauto listens for WeChat messages and calls the AstrBot Open API, so the WeChat bot and the QQ bot share one LLM and one LivingMemory — a conversation started on either platform is known on the other. It maps contacts by stable wxid so context survives nickname changes, replies in groups only when @-mentioned, ships a web control panel, and documents its fragile points honestly (the DirectUI send mechanism, the red-dot screenshot detection workaround).
bad: It depends on WeChat 3.9.x, which Tencent has server-side blocked: the README's own instructions require a memory patch (wechat_patcher.py) to bypass the version-too-low check after every WeChat restart, registry edits to stop auto-updates, and a double-scan login ritual. The UI automation competes for mouse/keyboard focus, and it is a single student author's 10-commit project with no releases.
didnt: Rejected — a fragile UI-automation bridge that only works by bypassing WeChat's version block; not a route we would ever take. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: jkroepke/okf-crossplane-v2
good: A structured OKF (Open Knowledge Format) v0.2 catalog for Crossplane v2: knowledge lives as small Markdown documents under catalog/ with OKF metadata, provenance in sources, keyed claim footnotes and relationships to related concepts, designed to be source-backed and version-aware. A self-hostable container ingests catalog/ into DuckDB and serves read-only MCP tools, including Crossplane package tools (get_versions, provider_crd_search, provider_crd_get_definition returning token-efficient YAML subtrees, examples and Terraform-docs lookup), with in-memory caching and fallback to the last successful catalog if ingestion fails.
bad: Entirely Crossplane/Kubernetes-specific in content and tooling. The README warns the public MCP server is a temporary early-access service whose availability is not guaranteed and which has no application-level authentication; self-hosting needs a container plus outbound HTTPS access to GitHub APIs, and OKF v0.2 is a young format pinned to okf-ingest 0.11.0.
didnt: Corroboration — its source-backed, version-aware catalog with provenance and keyed claim footnotes confirms our citation-locked, provenance-first page design; the Crossplane content itself is out of scope for a personal wiki. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: xerexcoded/pplx-cli
good: A CLI for Perplexity, NVIDIA NIM and OpenRouter with local, evidence-first RAG: BGE embeddings, SQLite FTS5 plus sqlite-vec hybrid search fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, and every result retaining source and chunk identifiers. Its native LLM Wiki compiles Markdown, text PDFs and captured web pages into cited, linked Markdown pages without moving source files, syncs idempotently, answers from raw source chunks with an instruction to report insufficient evidence rather than guess, exposes read-only MCP tools, ships a retrieval evaluation (Recall@k, MRR, nDCG), and renders a D3.js knowledge graph of a Markdown vault.
bad: Chat requires a paid provider API key, and wiki --web queries need a Perplexity API key even when another provider writes the local answer. Vector retrieval falls back to an exact in-process search if the sqlite-vec extension cannot load, and the README cautions that benchmark latency depends on corpus size, model and hardware rather than guaranteeing its speed claims.
didnt: Corroboration — hybrid FTS+vector retrieval with inspectable chunk provenance, abstention-oriented answering and a built-in retrieval eval confirms our retrieval and evaluation design; the provider-CLI surface duplicates our existing stack. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: guanyang/llm-wiki
good: An Obsidian + LLM personal knowledge base with equivalent schema files for Codex (AGENTS.md), Claude Code (CLAUDE.md) and Gemini (GEMINI.md), and detailed workflows held in progressively-disclosed Agent Skills. Beyond ingest/query/lint/publish it adds a knowledge lifecycle: per-page confidence scores (0.0-1.0) adjusted by source count, access frequency and Ebbinghaus-style decay, active/stale/archived state transitions, supersedes/superseded_by links, a four-tier consolidation model with explicit promotion thresholds, and web re-verification whose findings must be user-confirmed and persisted into the immutable raw/ layer before re-ingest.
bad: Very young and small: 7 commits since creation in April 2026, and the repo root holds only docs, raw, wiki, output and skills — it is a schema-and-skills specification with no executable engine, tests or evaluation of its own. Everything depends on the chosen LLM agent following the instructions and on Obsidian configuration and community plugins for the browsing experience.
didnt: Board — the lifecycle model (confidence decay curves, tier-promotion thresholds such as synthesis confidence at or above 0.85 suggesting publication) as a candidate refinement for claim-lifecycle scoring. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: zhurudong/andrej-karpathy-llm-wiki
licence: MIT (stated in the README License section; no LICENSE file in the repo root)
good: A minimal template whose entire 'program' is one CLAUDE.md file (with an AGENTS.md symlink for Codex/OpenCode): a one-line install.sh bootstraps raw/ (immutable articles) plus a wiki/ skeleton of summaries, entities, concepts, comparisons, overviews and synthesis, and the LLM then ingests URLs, answers index-first from wiki/_index.md, and lints for broken links, orphans, contradictions and stale claims — no backend, vector DB or RAG framework, and zero data migration when switching LLM tools.
bad: Template only: no code, search, tests or enforcement of any kind, so all behaviour depends on how faithfully an LLM follows a single prompt file. The repo has 11 commits and no releases, and the README claims MIT while the repo root contains no LICENSE file, leaving the licence grant less firmly documented than in comparable projects.
didnt: Corroboration — its two-layer immutable-raw/regenerable-wiki design with index-first querying confirms the core of our own wiki design; it is too minimal to supply anything beyond that confirmation. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: NeticSoul/wow-335a-addon-wiki
good: A worked LLM-Wiki compilation of the 34 chapters of 'World of Warcraft Programming' (2nd edition) into 64 interlinked pages: chapter summaries, 20 cross-referenced concept pages, condensed API/widget/event reference tables and sample-addon entity breakdowns, governed by a SCHEMA.md and navigable from an index.md that an LLM agent can be pointed at directly, or browsed as an Obsidian vault.
bad: A content-only wiki with no tooling, ingest pipeline or maintenance automation beyond its SCHEMA.md conventions, in a 9-commit repo. Its scope is deliberately narrow — WoW WotLK 3.3.5a (Interface 30300) only — and the README lists the modern Retail namespaces and functions that explicitly do not exist in that version.
didnt: Corroboration — a whole book compiled once into interlinked chapter, concept and reference pages confirms our compile-at-ingest approach for book-length sources; the game-addon content itself has no place in our wiki. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: norrietaylor/distillery
licence: Apache-2.0 (stated in the README License section; GitHub sidebar classifies the LICENSE as Other/NOASSERTION)
good: A team knowledge base delivered as 15 Claude Code skills (/distill with dedup detection, /recall semantic search with provenance, /pour multi-entry synthesis with citations, /watch and /radar feed monitoring, /gh-sync for GitHub issues/PRs, /investigate relationship traversal, among others), storing vector embeddings in DuckDB and retrieved conversationally via MCP over local stdio or a hosted HTTP service with GitHub OAuth. Default fastembed embeddings run offline with no API key (Jina/OpenAI optional), and the project is actively engineered: about 1,700 commits, 14 releases, tests, mypy --strict and ruff in its documented dev workflow.
bad: Team- and Claude-Code-centred: the plugin deliberately does not configure an MCP server automatically (a /setup wizard is required), and the hosted demo at distillery-mcp.fly.dev is explicitly for evaluation only — the README warns not to store sensitive or confidential data there. The licence position is ambiguous at source: the README claims Apache 2.0 while GitHub classifies the LICENSE file as Other/NOASSERTION.
didnt: Rejected — a team-brain scope and Claude Code skill surface that duplicate our own system, and the licence is ambiguous at source (README says Apache-2.0, GitHub classifies it Other/NOASSERTION), so its code is not adoptable. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: AliMahmoud15486/pm-llm-wiki
licence: MIT (stated in the README; a LICENSE file is present, though the GitHub sidebar classifies it as Other/NOASSERTION)
good: Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern specialised for product managers: a deliberately minimal model of four entity types — problem pages with evidence chains and mention counts, decision pages with options, evidence, rationale and explicit reversal conditions, an assumption register with dated status-flip history, and an open-questions queue tagged by resolution path from which interview scripts are generated. Three rituals (ingest, query, weekly lint as a 'product truth check') operate it, assumption/decision changes pass a write gate where the agent proposes and the human approves, deliverables such as PRDs are generated from cited evidence, and a complete worked pilot (FitLoop) is included.
bad: An immature snapshot: the repo has a single commit and no releases, and contains schema, templates and the pilot rather than any code, tests or tooling. It is PM-domain-specific and, by its own account, costs about 30 focused minutes of human discipline per week to keep fed and linted.
didnt: Board — decision pages carrying explicit reversal conditions, and an assumption register whose every status flip is dated with the source that caused it, as schema ideas for decision tracking. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: kchyhj/sociology-wiki-template
good: An accuracy-first research wiki template for sociologists built around a three-layer verification protocol — local primary source, then web-downloaded primary-source PDF, then leave the section blank — with secondary sources (reviews, abstracts, Wikipedia, AI summaries) categorically excluded at every layer. Twelve binding rules operationalise it (source-only summarisation, cite only papers present in references/, unverifiable content is deleted rather than annotated, per-ingest verification metadata), a five-layer note model separates source-faithful literature notes from the researcher's synthesized atomic claims, and bundled scripts provide linting, auto-linking and a local RAG indexer; documentation is bilingual English/Korean.
bad: Deliberately slow and expensive: the README states the design prioritises citation accuracy over speed and token economy and warns that turning the template into a working wiki 'still requires substantial additional setup and ongoing verification'. It is sociology-specific and Claude-centric — its own caveat section says smaller/local models are not recommended for ingestion because they fill blanks instead of leaving them empty — and the PolyForm Noncommercial licence bars commercial use without a separate licence from the author.
didnt: Corroboration — its leave-blank-over-fabrication verification protocol, per-sentence self-interrogation and ban on plausibility labels confirm our scored-abstention and citation-locking discipline; the PolyForm Noncommercial licence makes its code ideas-only in any case. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: llmrix/llm-wiki-skill
good: A Claude Code skill that synthesises knowledge at ingest time: it ingests PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, Markdown and images (standalone images and charts/diagrams/screenshots understood via Claude vision, not just OCR) into wiki sources, entities, concepts and syntheses pages, flags contradictions with existing content, archives query answers, and builds a self-contained interactive graph.html from explicit wikilinks plus AI-inferred associations at confidence 0.5 or above. READMEs are provided in seven languages.
bad: Very early: 4 commits and no releases. It is Claude-only — multimodal understanding depends on Claude's vision — and the format extractors capture only text from documents, so figures critical to meaning must be re-ingested as standalone images; the README describes no search, evaluation or approval-gating beyond reading wiki/index.md at query time.
didnt: Rejected — it duplicates the LLM-wiki skill stack we already have (catalogue verdict ALREADY HAVE); its multimodal ingest and graph ideas are already covered and it supplies no missing capability. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: rarce/git-wiki
good: A Claude Code / Agent-Skills skill implementing the LLM-wiki pattern in a personal git repo the user owns: immutable sources, LLM-owned Markdown pages, index.md read first on every query and an append-only grep-friendly log.md, with lint for stale dates, orphans, broken links, index drift and contradictions. Search is on-device hybrid — BM25 plus vector plus LLM rerank via qmd, with no embeddings uploaded — and there is no server, SaaS or database; an installer scaffolds either a private GitHub repo or a local-only repo, and multiple wikis coexist via per-wiki named qmd indexes.
bad: It stands on external moving parts: qmd must be installed on PATH, the GitHub CLI must be authenticated for GitHub-backed installs, and node/npm are required for the skills installer, which is delivered as a curl-piped shell script. This repo hosts only the skill, not a wiki, and retrieval quality is entirely delegated to the third-party qmd tool.
didnt: Rejected — it duplicates our existing git-backed wiki with hybrid search (catalogue verdict ALREADY HAVE); adopting it would add the qmd runtime dependency without supplying a capability we lack. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: zach22-1999/seller-second-brain
good: A Chinese-language hands-on book (v2.0, 79-page PDF plus HTML and Markdown editions) showing Amazon cross-border sellers how to build an AI-native second brain with GBrain: it compares the RAG, LLM Wiki and GBrain routes, then walks through page-first design, business knowledge objects, schema, resolver, Skill/MCP workflows, sync/embed/query/eval, a low-risk path from 20 knowledge samples to a review MVP, and write-boundary governance, all with real commands and worked examples aimed at non-engineers.
bad: It is a book, not software: the repo (3 commits) contains the manuscript and its exports, no runnable system, and the engine it teaches is the third-party garrytan/gbrain project rather than anything in this repo. Content is Chinese-only and narrowly aimed at cross-border ecommerce sellers, and the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence bars commercial reuse and imposes share-alike on derivatives.
didnt: Rejected — a domain how-to book for Amazon sellers built on a third-party engine, not a tool or method missing from our stack, and its CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence restricts reuse. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: hereisSwapnil/memwiki
good: A zero-dependency persistent-memory protocol for AI coding agents, installed with one 'npx memwiki init': it creates a .memory/wiki with a hot.md hot cache (about 500 words of recent context and next steps that agents read first), index, log, stack, patterns, bugs and decisions files, an immutable .memory/.raw/ for human-dropped sources, and hook files (.cursorrules, CLAUDE.md, Copilot instructions) that route Cursor, Claude Code and Copilot to the same shared memory. AGENTS.md instructs agents to update the wiki autonomously, offers /memwiki-ingest, /memwiki-lint and /memwiki-fold commands, and 'memwiki update' refreshes protocol files without touching the memory contents.
bad: No licence is stated in the repo — there is no LICENSE file in the root and the README text names none — so reuse terms are undefined. It is very new and small (9 commits), and the whole mechanism is prompt-level: correctness depends on each agent obeying AGENTS.md, with no search index, verification or enforcement code beyond the scaffolding; its scope is per-project coding memory, not general knowledge.
didnt: Board — the hot.md hot-cache pattern (a short recent-context-and-next-steps file read first each session) as a lightweight session-resume idea for project memory. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: mambo-wang/CodeWiki-Plus
good: A repository knowledge engine that splits upstream CodeWiki's black-box generation into 53 fine-grained MCP tools driven entirely by the AI IDE's own model — zero LLM API configuration — over a Tree-sitter AST and dependency-graph toolchain. On top of doc generation it adds evidence-based assertions with code references and confidence tiers (strong/weak/shadow), conflict dossiers for contradictory notes, cross-session task memory, team telemetry on knowledge use outcomes, method-level content-hash incremental updates, monorepo cross-service analysis, BM25 plus wikilink multi-hop search with a progressive reading protocol, 25 lint checks with a health score, and OKF v0.2-compatible structured wiki layout.
bad: Scoped to code repositories inside MCP-capable AI IDEs, not personal knowledge, and heavy: Python 3.12+ is required, Mermaid validation silently skips if Node.js is absent, the default branch is develop across about 1,300 commits of rapidly moving surface, and its team-memory/telemetry machinery brings credential and identity-resolution complexity documented at length in the README. Default output language is Chinese.
didnt: Board — confidence-tiered evidence assertions (strong/weak/shadow) paired with explicit conflict dossiers and outcome telemetry as candidate ideas for grading and adjudicating contested claims. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: djolex999/vir
good: Builds a Karpathy-style LLM Wiki automatically from Claude Code and Codex session transcripts (plus clipped web articles and PDFs) into a plain-Markdown, Obsidian-native vault of typed notes — patterns, gotchas, decisions, tools. Its quality controls are unusually explicit: structural transcript filtering with every skip recorded and reversible, confidence scores in note frontmatter with sessions at or below 0.6 dropped before distillation, an approve/edit/reject review loop that boosts verified notes in retrieval, recurring-lesson detection that proposes CLAUDE.md rules only with per-rule human confirmation and verbatim-quote checking, a retrieval eval behind its ranking defaults, dry-run cost estimates, and an MCP server exposing the vault mid-session.
bad: Its input universe is coding-agent sessions: Cursor support is only planned, Codex's no-API-key codex-cli provider is labelled experimental, and archived Codex threads are out of reach because only ~/.codex/sessions is read. The README itself concedes auto-distilled notes can be wrong and would be treated as truth by the agent without its layered controls, and distillation spends real model/API money (Haiku classification plus Sonnet distillation) unless a subscription CLI route is used.
didnt: Rejected — it is centred on mining coding-session transcripts, a source class our programme does not use as the personal wiki's input, and its vault/MCP surface duplicates our existing wiki stack. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: FeeiCN/FEEI.CN
licence: No open-source licence granted (README usage-boundary section: code may be read and learned from, but copying, modification, distribution or commercial use requires contacting the author first)
good: A long-maintained (about 3,300 commits) public personal knowledge, data and judgement system published as a Docusaurus site: 600+ Markdown/MDX documents on security and life systems, structured-data dashboards for reading, health, travel footprint, assets and multi-model LLM usage, local Docusaurus plugins and search extensions, and GitHub Actions deployment over SSH to Nginx, with documented local build, typecheck and docs-check commands.
bad: It is one person's public website, not a reusable wiki tool or engine. The README's usage-boundary section states the repo grants no open-source licence for the code and reserves rights over articles, personal data and media; some media lives only on the deployment server rather than in git, and several sync scripts depend on private credentials, GitHub Variables, iPhone apps and personal account authorisations, so the system cannot run standalone for anyone else.
didnt: Rejected — a personal Docusaurus publishing site with no licence granted and personally-bound data pipelines; at most its public data dashboards are a presentation-layer reference, not a knowledge engine for our private local-first wiki. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: EvelynnYu/MIRROW
licence: MIT (root licence; shared-cochlea derived files are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 per the README licence supplement)
good: Single-user, locally deployed AI companion core and app: a Memory V2 layer with immutable events, source tracing and revisable cognition books, a context builder that keeps source material and execution contracts separate, a persistent daydream/wander runtime, and a local app tying chat, diary, daily settlement and memory retrieval together — all model-agnostic via injected call_llm_func callbacks.
bad: Very young and single-author (created 2026-07, 14 commits, no releases), and companion-scoped rather than a knowledge system: the README states the public repo is not the production mirror — private identity, voice, group chat and device services are withheld — and the reference implementation is Windows-first. The licence is not cleanly MIT either: shared-cochlea derived files sit under non-commercial CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
didnt: Rejected — an AI-companion system, not a knowledge OS; its Memory V2 source tracing corroborates our raw-layer provenance discipline, but the persona/companion scope and the CC BY-NC-SA carve-out leave nothing for our stack (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: sdyckjq-lab/llm-wiki-skill
good: The most-adopted Karpathy-pattern implementation in this wave: a monorepo shipping the same wiki format as an installable Skill for Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw and Hermes plus a developer workbench, with confidence labels (EXTRACTED / INFERRED / AMBIGUOUS / UNVERIFIED), SHA256 dedupe with write-through cache updates, script-validated ingest formats, health checks for orphans, broken links and contradictions, and a fully offline interactive knowledge-graph HTML export.
bad: Verification stops at labelling: there is no citation locking, no scored abstention and no approval gate on writes, so a confident-sounding page and a sourced page differ only by a tag. The workbench half is explicitly a developer preview, the feature surface is very broad, and several extractors (WeChat, Xiaohongshu, login-gated pages) depend on extra tooling or a logged-in Chrome session.
didnt: Corroboration — its confidence labelling, ingest format validation, SHA256 dedupe and orphan/contradiction health checks independently parallel our design; the catalogue verdict already read ALREADY HAVE, and its verification model is weaker than our citation lockfile (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: WuKongOpenSource/Wukong_KnowledgeBase
licence: Custom licence (LICENSE.txt; GitHub detects Other / NOASSERTION)
good: A team knowledge-base module from the Wukong CRM suite: template-driven document creation (built-in templates for requirements, meeting notes, decision records, how-tos, retrospectives and work plans), online editing, article comments, external share links and global content search, on a Spring Cloud Alibaba + Vue stack with the frontend pre-bundled.
bad: Not a standalone product: it is one module of the 72crm suite, needs JDK + MySQL + Redis + Elasticsearch (README recommends ≥16 GB RAM) and a Wukong ID account whose appId/accessKey/secretKey must be pasted into the config. Only 13 commits since 2023, no AI or LLM features at all, and the licence is a custom non-OSI text.
didnt: Rejected — an enterprise CRM module with a heavy Java stack and a vendor-account dependency; no AI layer and nothing a personal local-first wiki can use (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: landlessway/spt-lifeos
good: A clean five-layer second-brain architecture published as an Obsidian vault: core identity layer (TELOS/CONTEXT/PROFILE loaded at session start), an evolution layer where agents deposit their best output, input layers (iBooks highlights, web clips, fragments, guided reading), a processing layer that decomposes old content into five reusable unit types — question, concept, opinion, case, solution — and output layers for writing and expression, with a processing tracker so old material is never re-processed.
bad: A folder convention, not a system: the entire repo is a single commit with no code, tests, evaluation or verification machinery — no citations, no contradiction handling beyond folder discipline, and its behaviour depends entirely on whichever agent the user points at the vault.
didnt: Board — the five-type content-unit taxonomy (question / concept / opinion / case / solution) as a page-typing idea for the compiled layer; the repo itself is a template with nothing to adopt (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: hujingjian/NoteFlow.Studio
good: A local Windows desktop tool that turns saved self-media videos (Bilibili / Douyin / YouTube) into knowledge: it extracts subtitles, copy and screenshots, uses any OpenAI-compatible model to clean and structure them into Markdown, and archives the result into an Obsidian vault in one click, with a ready-to-run release build for non-developers.
bad: Windows-only by construction (C# WPF + CefSharp), and deliberately shallow past capture: the README states RAG and vector search were removed, so generated notes carry no retrieval, no citation grounding and no verification. Young and single-author (10 commits, 11 stars).
didnt: Corroboration — video-to-transcript-to-structured-note ingest confirms the media-capture input class our clipper covers; the tool itself is a Windows desktop app outside our stack (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: kangers/gongji-obsidian-claude
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (content licence, per README licence section)
good: A complete worked instance of the Karpathy pattern in an unrelated domain — Chinese civil-service exam preparation: immutable raw/, a wiki/ of concept, entity and strategy pages maintained per an LLM-WORKFLOW.md schema, 4,000+ exam points, 20 subject question banks, 14 full mock papers with answers, error-note cards and SVG memory maps, published as a searchable MkDocs site; on ingest the AI updates concept and entity pages and flags contradictions between old and new material.
bad: It is a content corpus, not tooling: nothing here is reusable machinery, the exam content is time-sensitive by the repo's own disclaimer, and CC BY-SA share-alike would follow any adapted content. Eleven commits and a single maintainer.
didnt: Corroboration — an independent raw/wiki/schema instantiation in exam prep confirms the pattern generalises beyond our domain; content, not machinery, so nothing to take (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: yunshi1016/snapmind
good: Screenshot-first capture with near-zero friction: one global hotkey, region select, an annotation box for your own thought, then a multimodal model produces title, summary, tags and OCR text and writes structured Markdown (frontmatter, no embedded image) into a local Obsidian vault — automatically recording provenance (source app, window title, web URL) and degrading gracefully so a note is saved even if the AI call fails. Native implementations on Windows (Flutter) and macOS (SwiftUI, zero third-party dependencies).
bad: GPL-3.0 copyleft makes its code ideas-only for us. It is v0.1 with 16 commits, capture is desktop-only, and the AI-generated note is accepted as-is — provenance is recorded but nothing verifies the note against the screenshot or locks it to its source.
didnt: Board — capture-time provenance (source app, window title and URL recorded automatically with the note) as an enhancement idea for our clipper; GPL-3.0 makes the code itself ideas-only (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: xuxuyouxiu/PodMuse
good: A complete podcast-to-knowledge-base pipeline in an Electron app: paste a link from Xiaoyuzhou, Bilibili, Ximalaya, Apple Podcasts, Douyin or YouTube and it transcribes locally with Whisper (or takes platform subtitles), then generates a one-line summary, key viewpoints, quotes, a glossary and auto-interlinked entity cards for people, projects, concepts and terms; subscriptions auto-track new episodes, and RAG Q&A over the vault answers with cited sources. Notes land as standard Markdown in the user's own vault, with PDF and share-card export and Notion/Logseq sync.
bad: Citations are answer-level decoration: there is no source locking, no abstention when the vault lacks evidence, and auto-extracted entity cards are never verified. Actively released (137 releases) but a single author with 3 stars, and the installer targets Windows first.
didnt: Corroboration — audio ingest with automatic entity filing, backlinks and cited Q&A parallels our media capture and Ask design, minus the verification layer that is our differentiator (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: NCZkevin/chatglm-web
good: A self-hostable ChatGLM-6B chat front end from 2023 (FastAPI + Vue3, forked from chatgpt-web): streaming output, front-end parameter tuning, context selection, conversation image export and fully offline/intranet operation with your own fine-tuned GLM model.
bad: A period piece: it targets the superseded ChatGLM-6B (13 GB GPU memory at FP16), its own roadmap leaves the LangChain knowledge-base Q&A item unchecked — the knowledge feature was never implemented — Docker packaging is marked 'to be updated', and the repo has seen 21 commits since 2023.
didnt: Rejected — a 2023 chat UI for a superseded model whose knowledge-base Q&A was never built; nothing in it serves a knowledge OS (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: oadank/memory-qdrant
licence: MIT (stated in the README licence section; no LICENSE file at the source)
good: A three-layer long-term memory plugin for OpenClaw with a clean tiering story: SQLite holds raw conversation text, Qdrant holds vectors for semantic retrieval, and PostgreSQL/Apache AGE holds an entity-relation graph, offered as lite (SQLite), standard (+Qdrant) and full (+AGE) tiers with one docker-compose startup, a bearer-authenticated store/search/delete/summarise API, and a web admin UI with per-layer counts and service health.
bad: Memory is stored and recalled by similarity alone — no provenance, citation or abstention discipline — and the README's own examples ship default credentials (a default API token and database password) users are expected to change. Twenty-two commits, 8 stars, and semantic search silently returns little until an embedding model is configured.
didnt: Corroboration — its raw-text / vector / graph layering parallels our raw layer, hybrid retrieval and graph export; nothing taken, and its default-credential examples show the custody gaps our gateway defaults deny (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: kesepain-KE/kemo-agent
good: A substantial local, multi-user agent runtime (673 commits, versioned 1.5.0) built around a 'Tidal Engram' lifecycle memory: per-user SQLite memory stores with daily-weighted evidence, duplicate merging gated by a coverage threshold, and explainable scored retrieval across four lifecycle layers that returns matched fields, hit words, coverage and score. Task plans are created, approved, paused and resumed through an explicit state machine that the agent cannot run past, workspaces are isolated per user, and skills, cron, sub-agents and contract tests are built in.
bad: Very young (created 2026-07) and single-maintainer, with sprawling scope split across sibling repos (gateway, graph, Android app). The README itself concedes the remote install channels only work once release artefacts are separately published, and its memory is conversational — nothing is citation-locked to sources the way our compiled layer is.
didnt: Corroboration — its plan-approval state machine and lifecycle memory with explainable, coverage-scored retrieval independently confirm two of our core designs (approval-gated action; scored retrieval with stated coverage) (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: DeliveryPerson2004/Pantheon-of-Confidants
good: A from-scratch, strongly typed multi-agent runtime in TypeScript: a hand-built agent loop over the DeepSeek Responses API with tool-result backfill, a real A2A 1.0 peer network (Agent Cards, discovery, task delegation and result acceptance), and disciplined least-privilege boundaries — tools are registered per agent with Zod-validated inputs, only one agent is publicly exposed while the rest listen on loopback only, and the memo agent works inside an isolated E2B sandbox. SQLite session persistence, an isolated automated test suite, and an unusually honest separation of implemented features from roadmap.
bad: A learning playground, by its own framing: no releases, and the GraphRAG long-term memory that headlines its ambitions is explicitly still in the design stage, as is the MCP client. With no licence stated, none of its code is reusable by default.
didnt: Board — the least-privilege A2A pattern (one public agent card, loopback-only internal agents, per-role validated tools) as a design reference for the hosted-door question; the missing licence bars code reuse in any case (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: modemneko/LTMGraph
good: A LangGraph long-term-memory agent whose retrieval node is documented in unusual detail: intent- and topic-aware retrieval with dynamic k and type filtering, and an explicit scoring formula — weight = cosine similarity x time decay (0.95^days) x usage boost (1 + uses/10) — with a hard 0.3 threshold, plus periodic consolidation and reflection passes that extract observations and check them for contradictions.
bad: Abandoned by its own author: the README states the architecture was dropped for compute cost and lack of optimisation and is kept only as a reference for the ideas. Thirteen commits, Gemini-locked (LLM, embeddings and search all Google), and no evaluation of whether the weighting actually retrieves better.
didnt: Board — the explicit retrieval weighting (similarity x recency decay x usage boost, thresholded) as a documented reference point for our hybrid ranker; the system itself is abandoned (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: guoyihub/metacode-cli
good: A Java coding-agent CLI on the AgentScope Harness that deliberately mirrors Claude Code's mental model: plan mode with plan approval, tool-call confirmation before execution, MCP tools with lazy background loading and per-server timing diagnostics, context compaction at a configurable threshold, skills, and a workspace long-term memory — reusing the user's existing ~/.claude and ~/.codex credentials across Anthropic and OpenAI channels, with filesystem modes from rooted to sandboxed to Docker.
bad: The entire codebase landed in a single commit, so there is no verifiable development history; the default filesystem mode is UNRESTRICTED (execute requires confirmation, reads do not); there are deliberately no unit tests (regression is smoke scripts); and with no licence stated anywhere at the source, the code is all-rights-reserved regardless.
didnt: Corroboration — plan approval plus per-tool confirmation in a coding CLI mirror our approval-gated writes; nothing could be taken even if wanted, as no licence is stated (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: PerFluent/AdaMem-Implementation
good: An unofficial but complete engineering implementation of the AdaMem paper (Tsinghua + WeChat, 2026): messages are structurally parsed (summary, topics, facts, preferences, time anchors, participants) into per-participant working memory, then consolidated in three stages into episodic, persona, abstract and graph memory; at question time a route planner decides which layers to query, a multi-round research-reflection loop judges evidence coverage and issues follow-up queries, and the answer module is constrained to answer only from retrieved evidence with citation-mapping validation. A LoCoMo benchmark runner is included.
bad: A single-commit reproduction whose own README is candid that the full LoCoMo benchmark has not finished running and that stability, performance and consistency testing for production is still missing; the stack is heavy (LangGraph, mem0, Qdrant, Neo4j/Graphiti, BERTopic) and multi-stage ingest is slow and costly per conversation.
didnt: Corroboration — its evidence-coverage reflection loop and citation-checked, evidence-only answering are the closest external parallel in this wave to our abstention and evidence discipline; unproven at benchmark, so nothing taken (completion pass, 2026-10-21)
institution: Tsinghua University / WeChat (authors of the AdaMem paper this repo implements)

name: fengqiaozhu/own-mem0
good: An MCP server that exposes Mem0 long-term memory to any MCP client through three tools (save_memory, get_all_memories, search_memories), with configurable embedding models and dimensions, a PostgreSQL vector store, SSE and stdio transports, Docker deployment, and a connection manager with pooling and periodic cleanup to prevent connection leaks.
bad: A thin wrapper: all memory intelligence is upstream Mem0, and the server adds no provenance, citation or approval discipline of its own. Four commits, no releases, and the SSE transport binds 0.0.0.0 with no authentication in the design.
didnt: Rejected — a Mem0 wrapper that adds an unauthenticated write path; our MCP door is read-only and citation-bound by design (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: tingfeng347/windcode
good: A terminal coding agent built around auditability: four switchable permission modes, risk scoring by tool side-effect, command, working directory, network need and sandbox state, OS sandboxes (Bubblewrap on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS), decision hooks that can deny or tighten operations, sub-agents working in isolated git worktrees whose commits and verification results are checked before the parent integrates, run budgets, full trace recording, and a long-term memory whose candidates need confirmation — experiences and SOPs are only solidified from real changes plus verification results. Published on PyPI with 18 releases.
bad: Very young and single-maintainer (created 2026-07, 4 stars), and on Windows the OS sandbox deterministically degrades to danger_full_access, leaving only the permission layer. Its memory is per-project development memory, not a knowledge store.
didnt: Corroboration — candidate-gated memory (unverified conclusions are not solidified) and verifier-checked subagent integration independently match our custody design (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: feixing-Aemeath/I-miss-v0.5
good: A local-first long-term memory service that splits conversations, Markdown and wiki content into traceable atomic memories retaining source, type, importance and entities, then retrieves through Chroma vectors + SQLite FTS5 + an entity graph with one unified rerank (recency, importance, task utility, temporal validity, token budget). It supports feedback-driven utility updates, consolidation, time decay, SHA-256 incremental sync and Markdown sync for human review, and it publishes its offline regression honestly: 161 wiki files processed into 5,303 atomic memories with Recall@3 of 17/20.
bad: A research baseline, by its own statement: no CI, tags or releases, the formal DeepSeek + BGE-M3 acceptance run has not been done (the README refuses to claim it), and the recorded regression carried only 5 evidence anchors across 5,303 memories — provenance exists but citation grounding is thin.
didnt: Corroboration — provenance-carrying atomic memory with feedback-driven utility updates and hash-based incremental sync parallels our design; its own acceptance log shows the formal evaluation is unfinished (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: zhaoquan219/open_deepagents
good: A FastAPI + Vue scaffold for DeepAgents applications with a deliberately small, well-fenced runtime surface: per-user session isolation, a SQL product ledger (users / sessions / runs / uploads / ordered events), recursive agent packages (prompts, tools, middleware, skills, memory, sub-agents) whose file access is governed by native path-scoped permissions — read and write operations granted per path — sandbox profiles defaulting to 'safe' with uploads mounted read-only, shared SSE contracts, and scaffold/contract verification tooling.
bad: A scaffold, not a product: 2 commits, no releases, and the 'shell' sandbox profile runs commands directly on the host. No licence is stated anywhere at the source, so nothing in it is reusable by default.
didnt: Corroboration — path-scoped operation permissions declared inside the agent package mirror our gateway scope model; an unlicensed scaffold, so nothing taken (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Coco AI
licence: MIT (app); the separate Coco Server component is AGPL-3.0
good: INFINI Labs' unified search platform: one Tauri/Rust cross-platform app (desktop and mobile) searching across Google Workspace, Dropbox, Confluence, GitHub and other connected sources with relevance ranking and intent understanding, plus a Gen-AI team chat over the connected enterprise knowledge and private-deployment options. Mature by this wave's standards — 1,003 commits, 726 stars, 13 releases.
bad: An enterprise team product: its value sits in the connector fleet and the AGPL-3.0 Coco Server rather than in a personal, local-first knowledge layer, and its chat answers carry no citation locking or abstention discipline.
didnt: Corroboration — unified multi-source search with a team assistant is the enterprise end of the Lens search spectrum; the AGPL server and team scope keep it reference-only (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: mcp-gitee
good: Gitee's official MCP server (Go, by oschina): a full tool surface over Gitee repositories, issues, pull requests and notifications for personal, organisation and enterprise accounts, with dynamic toolset enable/disable (whitelist and blacklist flags), a configurable API base for other Gitee instances, stdio/SSE/HTTP transports, an official hosted remote endpoint and npx distribution.
bad: A live, write-capable door onto a forge — create_repo, merge_pull, create_release — gated only by the caller's personal access token, the inverse of a default-deny gateway; and it serves one forge only.
didnt: Corroboration — an official forge MCP server with dynamic toolset toggling parallels our gateway tool scoping; its token-only write access shows exactly what default-deny adds (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: sanhuaz/M200_Agent
good: A single-user local agent (FastAPI + LangGraph + Vue 3) with three-layer memory — role rules, structured user facts, vector semantic memory — and hybrid document retrieval (Chroma + SQLite FTS5/jieba fused by RRF, optional reranker that degrades explicitly rather than faking success). Its MCP handling is unusually careful: servers are disabled by default, tools enter the registry only after per-item administrator authorisation under an owner_only policy, secrets live only as environment references, and relationship memory stays off until the user authorises it once. A 150-question RAG evaluation is recorded in its changelog.
bad: No licence is stated anywhere at the source. Scope sprawls well past knowledge work (an emotional-companion loop, comic download tasks), the surface is QQ-centric, and it has a single star.
didnt: Corroboration — per-item MCP authorisation with owner-only defaults and honest degradation mirror our gateway discipline; the code is unlicensed (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: LZL-LLL/agent
good: Presents the CowAgent design: a proactive personal assistant with autonomous task planning, layered long-term memory (core memory, daily memory and 'dream distillation') with keyword and vector retrieval, a conversationally managed knowledge base, a skill system with one-click Skill Hub installs and dialogue-created skills, multimodal messages and 24/7 multi-channel operation (WeChat, Feishu, DingTalk, QQ, web).
bad: This listing is a 6-commit re-upload of someone else's project: the README's clone instructions and Docker image both point at zhayujie's repositories, so nothing here distinguishes it from the original, which the survey covers in its own right.
didnt: Rejected — a mirror of zhayujie/CowAgent, already covered as the original; this copy adds nothing (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: sameencai/Karvis
good: A personal life assistant running on WeCom (deployable to Tencent Cloud SCF) that keeps every byte as Markdown in the user's own folders: all messages archived raw to Quick-Notes, a long-term memory.md, and a decisions.jsonl decision log whose entries resurface automatically after N days for review. Three-tier model routing (Qwen Flash / DeepSeek main / DeepSeek-R1 think) with graceful degradation, 31 skills across notes, todos, habits, reading and review reports, and a five-layer anti-nagging design governing when it may proactively speak.
bad: Personal-assistant scope: memory is a single memory.md plus the message archive — no compiled knowledge layer, no citations, no verification — and the full mode chains WeCom, Tencent Cloud and OneDrive. Fifteen commits, single author.
didnt: Corroboration — decision logging with scheduled review and raw-capture-to-Markdown filing parallel our conversation-log and filing discipline (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: LucasIdeal/personal-agent
licence: MIT (per the README licence section; no LICENSE file at the source)
good: A small Node web assistant (chat, todos, subscription reminders, long-term memory, capability extensions) with per-user runtime instances and data directories, keys kept only in the local .dsh/ store, and a written technical report covering memory write/retrieval, multi-turn context and token control, tool routing, LLM fallback and user isolation.
bad: Identity is a typed English name — the README itself states it is not a password or authentication — so the per-user isolation is organisational, not a security boundary. Ten commits and no releases.
didnt: Rejected — a hobby-scale assistant whose isolation is weaker than our custody model; nothing in it advances the knowledge layer (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: FuGuiGuaGua/PersonAgent
good: An AgentScope-based travel assistant (Aligo) with a plan-and-execute architecture: LLM semantic intent recognition across six intent classes, sub-agents refactored as lazily loaded skill plugins with progressive disclosure (metadata only at routing time), a two-layer memory design, Milvus + BGE RAG that returns document sources for traceability, priority-parallel scheduling, and resilience machinery (circuit breaker, exponential-backoff retry, health checks).
bad: The README's own notes admit the headline storage is aspirational: PostgreSQL and Redis are the production design, while the current version keeps long-term memory in JSON files. Its accuracy figures (90% intent, 95% RAG) are self-reported with no published evaluation set, and the whole system is a Doubao-locked travel demo in 2 commits.
didnt: Rejected — a travel-planning demo whose production memory layer is unimplemented; nothing in it serves a knowledge OS (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: waterlikesky/super-assistant-system
good: An unusually honest M0 skeleton for a multi-channel personal assistant: a unified event/message schema across WeChat, DingTalk, email and SMS, read-only connectors with outbound messaging off by default, redaction inside the ingest pipeline (normalise → desensitise → store), privacy boundaries stated up front (no default upload of full chats, keys never in git, enterprise and personal data isolated), and a research conclusion against dumping entire chat histories into a knowledge base — the loop should be summarise → extract facts → write memory → retrieve.
bad: Almost nothing is implemented: real channel ingestion (M1), the memory layer (M2) and the learning loop (M3) are all future milestones, and the connectors are interface placeholders. Four commits.
didnt: Corroboration — read-only-by-default channel ingest with outbound off and pipeline redaction parallels our connector custody; a skeleton, so nothing to take (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: chenkx612/personal-agent-with-memory-and-tools
good: A LangGraph ReAct personal assistant running two independent FAISS-backed RAG stores — a user-profile memory whose JSON file is the declared source of truth (with mtime-checked index caching) and a notes store with incremental indexing — plus LangGraph SQLite checkpointing for cross-session context, and human-in-the-loop confirmation required before the add_note tool executes.
bad: Roleplay-oriented hobby scope, and its memory maintenance is unverified: update and /tidy merges are LLM-driven with no source checking. No licence is stated anywhere at the source, and it has no stars or releases.
didnt: Rejected — a roleplay-oriented assistant; the confirm-before-note pattern is familiar and its memory layer carries no verification (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: isolat-3k/dsh-memory
good: A memory plugin for the DeepSeek Harness with a bounded, inspectable design: a human-editable SOUL.md injected as long-term context at session start, and per-session 'handles' — length-capped compressed memories written by a dedicated memory sub-agent into handles.json under explicit budgets (4,000 chars total, 600 per handle, 100 sessions, oldest evicted first), with hash tracking to avoid re-injecting what a session has seen, atomic serialised file writes, and a mock-context smoke test covering the core paths.
bad: A v0.1 design draft tied to a single harness: memory is plaintext Markdown/JSON with no encryption or sync, there is no browse/edit/review interface yet, and the compressed handles are model summaries that — by the README's own warning — may omit information or misstate it.
didnt: Corroboration — SOUL-file injection plus budgeted, hash-deduped cross-session handles parallel our standing-context files and lean-memory discipline (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: dbwang0130-tech/jarvis
licence: no licence — the README states the project licence is not yet determined
good: A Go terminal assistant over plain-text data — org-mode schedules, a ledger-cli plain-text account book, NDJSON health records, a memory.md — with risk-tiered autonomy: queries and reversible local organisation run automatically, while irreversible actions (sending mail, deleting) stop for confirmation, tunable via /auto off/clean/all. It speaks the Agent Client Protocol over stdio so other clients (including a phone app) can drive it, with permission requests surfaced to the client; secrets come from the system keychain or external commands, never config files; and its contributor rules require any new irreversible action to declare a risk level and ship confirmation-path tests.
bad: The licence is explicitly undecided (the README says so and there is no LICENSE file), so nothing is reusable. Early stage — data formats may still change — macOS-centric (launchd, keychain), and its long-term memory is a single user-stated-preferences file.
didnt: Corroboration — risk-tiered autonomy with confirmation for irreversible actions and keychain-held secrets mirrors our tiered delegation and custody rules; licence undecided, so nothing taken (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Nuru-Banmian/self-learning-agent
good: A multi-agent personal assistant whose memory discipline is the strictest in this wave: the learning agent has no write tool — it proposes memory candidates in a strict JSON schema, the application validates them and stores the user's own original sentences with their source message; potentially conflicting memories suspend BOTH sides pending clarification; corrections and deletions run through the same validated transaction with optimistic versioning, deleted memories cannot be re-taught from already-processed sources, and plan suggestions become todos only on explicit acceptance. A learning-transfer evidence panel with human checkpoints (passed / failed / unverified, default unverified) and per-issue acceptance records over ~187 tests document what was actually verified.
bad: Single-user, local-only and tied to one fixed model (Qwen via DashScope); its conservative Chinese statement parsing openly misses complex or paraphrased expression, and keyword-based memory loading can miss synonyms. No licence is stated anywhere at the source.
didnt: Corroboration — source-bound memory candidates, conflict suspension and acceptance-gated writes are the strongest external parallel in this wave to our memory custody rules (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: 1052666/1052-OS
good: A local-first personal agent OS (TypeScript/React + Express, 366 commits, 27 releases) with a tool registry that classifies every tool by read/write safety, side effects and confirmation need under three permission modes, and — most notably — a persistent multi-round research subsystem implementing a claim–evidence–review loop: web pages are extracted into immutable snapshots hashed with SHA-256, evidence must anchor to exact character offsets inside a snapshot, a claim auto-passes review only with at least two independent supporting sources and no contradicting evidence (single-source, conflicting or high-risk claims stop at needs_review), and wiki/PKM writeback re-checks review state and refuses to solidify pending or conflicted content. Context compaction is checkpoint-based with a summarisation fallback, and long-term memory has a separate sensitive tier.
bad: A whole personal OS, not a component: the surface is enormous (SQL workbench, SSH, flow orchestration, three chat-platform channels), and it rests on a single 17-year-old maintainer. Its wiki/memory layers serve the agent runtime rather than a curated, owner-edited knowledge base.
didnt: Corroboration — its claim–evidence–review writeback gate is the closest external implementation in this wave of our citation and claim discipline (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: lyxhnu/Skill-First-Hybrid-RAG
good: 'Ragclaw': a file-first, auditable agent workbench (FastAPI + LangGraph + Next.js) where conversations, tool calls and retrieval all land in local files, long-term memory is a directly editable MEMORY.md, and every skill is a readable SKILL.md. Its retrieval chain is skill-first with an evidence-sufficiency gate: curated skill evidence is tried first, and only when it returns partial / not_found / uncertain does the system fall back to vector + BM25 retrieval fused by RRF, answering with cited evidence while the frontend Inspector exposes retrieval steps, evidence sources, tool calls and raw messages. Ragas-based evaluation scripts and a retry-lesson-capture skill (failed attempts distilled into lessons) are built in.
bad: Only 2 commits and no licence stated anywhere, so despite the design quality nothing is reusable; the hybrid index covers Markdown/JSON only (Excel/PDF depend on the skill path), and the README itself bounds it as a local research workbench, not production.
didnt: Corroboration — skill-first retrieval gated by an explicit evidence-sufficiency check mirrors our Ask routing discipline (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: xinghuangjun/YiYan
good: A single-file tkinter chat client whose memory scheme is documented with unusual precision: every N rounds the conversation is summarised into a Markdown file of numbered memory entries, each annotated with T (normalised age) and L (normalised length) combined as W = k·T + (1-k)·L, and W governs compression and deletion; entries are immutable once written (only T/L are recomputed), periodic 'review' passes re-inject the accumulated entries in original order, and an offline self-test runs against a mock server with no network or UI.
bad: A single-session chat toy (3 commits, days old): memory is lossy rolling summaries — entries are model-written digests with no path back to raw conversation beyond the summary files — and the README discloses the API key is stored in plaintext in the local config.
didnt: Board — the explicit W = k·time + (1-k)·length weighting with immutable entries as a documented memory-decay reference; companion-chat scope (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Li-kaige/chatgpt-vits-waifu
good: A 2023 voice-companion project pairing the ChatGPT API with VITS speech synthesis: conversations are recorded to files in real time and resumed on the next run, and when the history exceeds the model's context limit the earlier conversation is automatically summarised and replaced by the summary, extending continuous long conversations; Japanese dialogue is auto-translated for Japanese VITS voices.
bad: A 2023 hobby project: the 'memory' is a saved transcript plus lossy summarisation with no provenance, and setup requires pasting API keys into the source file. Thirteen commits, no tests.
didnt: Rejected — a voice-companion toy whose memory is overflow summarisation; nothing for a knowledge system (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: shuakami/amyalmond_bot
good: A QQ group chatbot built on Tencent's official QQ Python SDK (avoiding unofficial-protocol ban risk), with long- and short-term memory management, automatic recognition and remembering of user names for personalised interaction, customisable prompts, administrator control commands, hot-reloadable configuration and detailed logging; 56 commits and 5 releases.
bad: A group-chat bot, not a knowledge system: its memory is conversational personalisation with no provenance or verification, and the MPL-2.0 file-level copyleft makes its code ideas-only for us in any case.
didnt: Rejected — a group-chat bot; nothing in it serves a knowledge OS (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: DreamDonghao/insoulforge
good: A C++23 OneBot chatbot backend (243 commits, 18 releases) with the most carefully specified memory maintenance in this wave: extracted person memories land in pending_entries carrying source and UTC write time, and a daily 03:00 consolidation merges them into stable_memory — deduplicating and correcting only on explicit evidence, deleting only the snapshot it processed, covering missed runs on startup, and deleting nothing when a run fails. Similarity thresholds govern merge (0.65) and passive injection (0.45), cross-session sharing defaults off, and reply routing is confidence-gated: a structured decision model answers first, and low confidence falls back to a router LLM.
bad: Companion/group-chat scope — affection scores are a first-class part of its memory — and AGPL-3.0 copyleft makes the code ideas-only for us. Its memory serves persona consistency, not knowledge, and none of it is citation-checked.
didnt: Corroboration — the pending-to-stable two-stage consolidation with failure-safe semantics and confidence-gated routing parallel our filings-to-compiled flow and abstention gates; AGPL makes it ideas-only regardless (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: 1437649480/miku-hermes-chat
good: A Hatsune Miku roleplay deployment on the Hermes Agent framework (a character SKILL.md, sticker-injection engine with an emotion-matched sticker catalogue and web manager, TTS options, WeChat gateway scripts, token auto-refresh and keep-awake operations scripts) whose sessions never auto-reset and whose long histories are compressed.
bad: Its model access is grey-area by construction — reverse proxies of the DeepSeek and Kimi web products — and the README itself warns the approach is unstable, risks account bans and urges readers to pay for the official API. The 'memory' is the host framework's session persistence; the repo adds no memory or knowledge machinery of its own.
didnt: Rejected — a roleplay wrapper over reverse-proxied free web APIs; nothing to learn for our stack (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: clearyss/WeLoom
good: A local-first chat-history memory system (pure Python stdlib + SQLite) that imports multi-platform chat exports, cleans them with a per-message audited cleaning_decisions record and quality scores, indexes terms + FTS5 + trigram with LIKE fallback, and generates long-term reports (per-person reports, a main report, a persona profile) through a pipeline with dry-run estimation and a report-doctor integrity check. Retrieval is evidence-first with a public trace (--show-trace), and every layer degrades gracefully (FTS unavailable → terms/LIKE; tool calls fail → local multi-round retrieval; report API fails → conservative fallback).
bad: AGPL-3.0 copyleft (ideas only), only 4 commits, and its purpose is persona distillation — building a high-fidelity replica of a person from their chats — which optimises for sounding like the person, with model-generated reports, rather than for source-faithful knowledge.
didnt: Corroboration — audited cleaning decisions and visible retrieval traces parallel our provenance discipline; the AGPL licence and clone aim keep it reference-only (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: qa296/astrbot_plugin_memora_connect
good: An AstrBot memory plugin modelled on the hippocampus: conversations are extracted into a weighted knowledge graph of element nodes (people, objects, places, behaviours, traits) whose association strengths update with use; recall runs five strategies at once (semantic vector, keyword, graph association, time weighting, strength ranking), and maintenance performs strength decay, automatic forgetting, periodic consolidation and similarity merging, with per-group memory isolation. 214 commits.
bad: Beta software mid-migration to a new graph architecture, and reconstructive by design: association strengths are rewritten by every conversation, so memory drifts from what was actually said — the opposite of source-faithful memory. No licence is stated anywhere at the source.
didnt: Rejected — a companion-bot memory plugin whose reconstructive graph contradicts source-faithful memory; unlicensed (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: adj18311/qq-bridge-plus
licence: MIT (code, inherited from upstream; LICENSE file adds a SnowLuma EULA notice — GitHub detects Other / NOASSERTION)
