good: A fully reproducible model merge: mergekit SLERP of two Gemma-2-9B fine-tunes (ArliAI RPMax and UCLA-AGI SPPO-Iter3) with the complete YAML recipe published, including a V-shaped layer-wise interpolation curve - anyone can rebuild the exact weights from the card.
bad: 'Memory' is only a name: this is a roleplay-oriented merge of two Gemma-2-9B fine-tunes with no memory mechanism, no evaluation, and no licence stated on the card. The merge config's own comment describes a different merge (Hermes/WizardMath), a copy-paste leftover that undermines confidence in the recipe as published.
didnt: Rejected - a name-collision merge with no memory content and no licence; recorded so the catalogue's memory sweep is not mistaken for coverage of memory systems. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: ClaudioItaly/Memory-9-Q4_K_M-GGUF
licence: no licence stated at source (the card frontmatter carries no license field).
good: The Q4_K_M GGUF conversion of the Memory-9 merge, ready for llama.cpp CLI/server with copy-paste invocation lines - the standard low-friction local-inference packaging for a 9B model.
bad: A format conversion of an unlicensed, unevaluated merge (see the Memory-9 row): the card adds nothing but run commands and defers to the original card for all model detail. No licence is stated here either.
didnt: Rejected - a GGUF repack of the Memory-9 merge; no independent content. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: cloudqi/cqi_brain_memory_question_anwser_pt_v0

bad: The card is visibly borrowed: its example code and links point to consciousAI's checkpoints, not this one, so the provenance of the reported scores for THIS upload is not clean. Extractive QA of this kind also returns spans with a confidence score and no citation discipline - the answer is only as checkable as the context you fed it.
didnt: Corroboration - recorded as a data point for the extractive pole of answering: span + confidence from a fixed context is the behaviour our Ask door generalises with citation locking and scored abstention on top; the model itself is not needed. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: cognitivetech/Mistral-7b-Inst-0.2-Bulleted-Notes_GGUF

A GGUF of a 2024-era 7B instruct model is also a fast-depreciating artefact.

name: Davlan/xlm-roberta-base-wikiann-ner

WikiANN is Wikipedia-derived silver data, so label noise is inherited; the card's own limitation restricts it to news-like text of a certain period.

name: Dream-W/ObsidianSmall-Base

didnt: Rejected - an architecture experiment (and another 'Obsidian' name collision); interesting as evidence that post-transformer block designs are being publicly checkpointed with honest scorecards, but there is nothing to adopt. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Duckets/Hy-Memory-30B-A3B-MLX-4bit

bad: A straight quantisation adds no capability over the original studied at B086, and it runs only on Apple Silicon through MLX - useless on our Linux VM. The flattering numbers are one vendor evaluation and one user's one-day shadow test, not independent benchmarks.

(completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Ferch423/gpt2-small-portuguese-wikipediabio
licence: MIT (declared in the card frontmatter under the misspelled key 'licence').

name: guell00/OBSIDIAN-9B-Coder
licence: no licence stated at source (verified by full-text search of the 1,426-line card: no license field and no licence statement).
good: A single-author coding model with an unusually serious dataset story: LoRA fine-tune specialised for complete, long-form implementations (whole single-file web apps, Three.js, Canvas) across 10 instruction languages, trained on the author's Coder Max corpus whose curation pipeline syntax-validates Python, strips credentials, API keys and local IPs, and stamps every record with SHA-256 provenance metadata.
bad: A 1,426-line card with zero benchmark results - every quality claim ('strong specialization') is asserted, none measured - and no licence stated anywhere in it despite the full-text search, so the weights' legal status is undefined. The base model is itself an obscure community fine-tune, two removes from any audited release.
didnt: Rejected - an unbenchmarked, unlicensed community coder (and a third 'Obsidian' name collision); its dataset pipeline, though - SHA-256 provenance per record and credential sanitisation before training - corroborates the provenance discipline our raw layer already follows. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: hebertgo/knowledgebase-intent-llm
good: A tidy example of the small-specialist pattern: a 1.5B Qwen2.5 (4-bit MLX) LoRA-fine-tuned on 5,000 examples to route a knowledge-management app's requests into a strict JSON intent - Search / Create / Clarify / Conversation plus content type and topic - small enough to run on-device in an iOS app via MLX Swift, with the exact output contract documented on the card.
bad: The card reports no accuracy or evaluation of any kind for the classifier, the action/content taxonomy is hard-wired to one app's three content types, and a 1.5B 4-bit model fused from 100 LoRA iterations is a fragile artefact to depend on. It solves a problem only inside its own app.
didnt: Rejected - a single-app intent router; our gateway routes intents with the main model under approval gates, and a 4-action taxonomy for videos/bookmarks/todos does not transfer. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: hhks/PonyXL_Notes_Backup

bad: 'Notes' here is a Rentry page's name, not note-taking: the artefact is anime image-generation LoRAs with an explicitly unknown licence, no documentation beyond two links, and no update since March 2024 - legally and practically unusable.

name: iZELX1/llm-wikipedia

didnt: Rejected - a style fine-tune whose failure mode (fluent, unfaithful encyclopaedia prose) is precisely what our citation-locked answering exists to prevent; recorded as the contrast case. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: jyohukuchan/Hy-Memory-30B-A3B-exl3-4.08bpw
licence: Apache-2.0 (per the card frontmatter and License and attribution section; matches the source weights, original LICENSE preserved).
good: The most rigorous quantisation card in this programme: a mixed-precision EXL3 conversion of Tencent's memory-writer with every precision allocation tabled, calibration methodology disclosed (including synthetic fictional memory-writing calibration examples, explicitly not user data), weight digests published, and - rarest of all - the failed initial validation preserved alongside the passing one, with a written analysis of why the first prompt failed.
bad: It runs only in ExLlamaV3 with a runtime fork fix, long-context behaviour is unvalidated, and the card is explicit that the smoke checks do not measure quality loss against BF16. The underlying capability question - whether a quantised writer still reconciles memory correctly - is answered with three checks, not a benchmark.
didnt: Corroboration - the strongest in this batch: its held-out checks test exactly our three hard cases (extraction, supersession replacement, abstention when evidence is absent), its preserved failed first run is our audit discipline in miniature, and its finding that a memory-writer keeps superseded facts unless the instruction demands currently-valid facts only independently corroborates our directional-supersession gap from the model side. The artefact itself - a third-party quant - is not adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: katarzynawozniak/retrieval-notes
licence: Apache-2.0 (per the card frontmatter and License section).
good: An honestly labelled research scaffold: a small EfficientFormer (nano, dilated attention, cross-attention fusion) implementation for retrieval, shipped with its generated config, default training recipe, and an initialisation checkpoint - with repeated, explicit statements that it is a reproducible starting point, not a trained release, plus a concrete evaluation protocol for whoever trains it.
bad: There is no trained model here: the checkpoint is an initialisation for smoke tests, the implementation is custom (generic loading APIs need an explicit adapter), and the architecture (an image-domain EfficientFormer variant) is aimed at image-text retrieval, not text knowledge retrieval.
didnt: Rejected - an untrained scaffold, not a retrieval system; its card is recorded as another instance of the honest-notes pattern (state what is unproven, prescribe the evaluation) that our own records follow. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: knowledge-computing/geolm-base-cased
licence: CC-BY-NC-2.0 (per the card frontmatter and Model Details).

bad: The card is a half-finished template: uses, training data detail, and all evaluation results are placeholders, so the model's quality must be taken from the paper, not the artefact page. The licence is CC-BY-NC-2.0 - an unusual, non-commercial licence for model weights that bars product use.
didnt: Rejected - licence (CC-BY-NC is ideas-only for us) and scope: geospatial encoding is a capability our text-and-citation stack does not need; the pretraining triad (OSM + Wikidata + Wikipedia) is noted as the standard recipe for grounding a model in the same public record we cite. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

didnt: Rejected - an undocumented re-upload of the GeoLM fine-tune under a non-commercial licence; nothing evidenced beyond the parent model's row. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: llm-book/bert-base-japanese-v3-ner-wikipedia-dataset

name: louis030195/multi-qa-MiniLM-L6-cos-v1-obsidian
licence: no licence stated at source (the card frontmatter carries pipeline tag and tags but no license field).
good: One of the few genuine Obsidian artefacts in this sweep: a MiniLM-L6 sentence-transformer fine-tuned on the author's own published brain/notes site, with the training code (obsidian-search) linked - a personal-vault embedding model, so semantic search over his notes uses representations adapted to his own writing rather than a generic corpus.

Our retrieval is keyword/citation-based today; a personal-vault embedding tune is a legitimate future experiment, recorded here with its provenance. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: louis030195/multi-qa-MiniLM-L6-cos-v1-obsidian-obsidian
licence: no licence stated at source (the card frontmatter carries no license field).

bad: A duplicate in everything but name: the doubled '-obsidian' suffix, the missing provenance line, and a near-identical training record make this read as an accidental re-upload of the sibling checkpoint. No licence stated, no evaluation published.

name: maxbennett/generalized-neural-memory-gnm-counterfact
licence: Meta Llama 3 Community License (card frontmatter 'llama3'; base model Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct).
good: The main model from a NeurIPS 2026 paper on controllable neural memory: a Llama-3-8B MemoryLLM trained with instruction-conditioned memorisation, so natural-language instructions in the document stream itself decide what gets learned - facts, response formats, even refusal policies - evaluated on the CounterFACT benchmark. It is the clearest statement in this sweep that 'what to remember' is becoming an instructed, auditable act rather than an accident of training.
bad: The card is a pointer, not a record: no results, no training detail, no usage beyond the repo's download script - every number lives in the paper. And the licence is Meta's Llama 3 community licence (custom terms), so the weights are not freely adoptable regardless.
didnt: Corroboration - the learned-memory field is converging on our governance shape from the other side: memory writes that are instruction-conditioned, selective, and able to learn refusal policies are exactly approval-gated writes and scored abstention, arrived at by training rather than by file discipline. Recorded as corroboration of the design direction; the model itself is not adoptable (Llama licence, research artefact). (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: maxbennett/generalized-neural-memory-gnm-counterfact-ablation
licence: Meta Llama 3 Community License (card frontmatter 'llama3'; base model Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct).
good: A properly published control condition: the GNM ablation in which gradients are blocked through the memorise step, so the model can learn to read memory but not to write it - the comparison that isolates how much of the main model's CounterFACT performance comes from learning what to write. Few research releases ship their ablations as first-class, downloadable artefacts.
bad: An ablation checkpoint has no standalone use - it exists to be compared against the main model - and its card, like the main model's, publishes no numbers. Same Llama community licence.
didnt: Rejected as an artefact; the method is the point - publishing the frozen-write control is how the paper proves the write policy itself carries the gains, the same evidentiary pattern our abstention battery and trust ledger implement for file-based memory. Recorded with the main GNM row's corroboration. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: maxbennett/generalized-neural-memory-iclft-counterfact
licence: Meta Llama 3 Community License (card frontmatter 'llama3'; base model Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct).
good: The honest control in the GNM paper's design: a Llama-3-8B fine-tuned on the same data and objective as the neural-memory model, but keeping documents and instructions in context instead of writing them to memory - the baseline that shows what learned memory adds over plain in-context learning on CounterFACT.
bad: A baseline exists to be beaten: by construction it has no persistent memory, so its long-horizon behaviour is bounded by the context window. The card publishes no scores, and the licence is Meta's Llama 3 community licence.
didnt: Rejected as an artefact; recorded as the third member of the GNM release set (main, write-ablation, ICL baseline) whose comparative design is the corroboration noted at B089 - the paper measures learned memory against exactly the in-context approach our file-based system resembles, and still ships the baseline openly. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: MemorySlices/Tartan-C-T-TSKH-spring540x960-M

bad: The card is a 26-line mixin stub: no dataset description, no endpoint-error numbers, no explanation of what the checkpoint name encodes (TartanAir split, spring scene, 540x960 resolution, M size must be inferred from the name and the linked repo). 'MemorySlices' is the HF organisation's name, not a memory technology.
didnt: Rejected - an optical-flow checkpoint swept in by an organisation name; the artefact's substance lives in the SEA-RAFT paper and repo, neither of which concerns knowledge systems. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)
institution: Princeton University (Princeton VL lab, via the SEA-RAFT library linked on the card)

name: MemorySlices/Tartan480x640-M
good: The 480x640-resolution variant of the SEA-RAFT TartanAir optical-flow checkpoint, under the same permissive BSD-3 licence and mixin distribution as its sibling - a matched pair for flow evaluation at two resolutions.
bad: Same stub card as its sibling - no metrics, no data description - and the two cards are literally interchangeable text under different checkpoint names, so nothing distinguishes this 480x640 variant's quality at the source.
didnt: Rejected - a second resolution variant of the SEA-RAFT Tartan checkpoint; recorded once with its sibling's reasoning. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)
institution: Princeton University (Princeton VL lab, via the SEA-RAFT library linked on the card)

name: Metin/Gemma-2-2B-TR-Knowledge-Graph
licence: Gemma (Google's Gemma licence terms, per the card frontmatter 'license: gemma'; base model google/gemma-2-2b-it).
good: A small model with a sharp specialisation: Gemma-2-2B-it LoRA-tuned on 30K synthetic samples to turn Turkish documents into structured knowledge graphs - typed nodes and named relationships emitted as JSON ready for a graph database - trained in 3 hours on a single GPU, triggered by a simple <knowledge_graph> prompt suffix, with complete worked examples on the card.
bad: No extraction-quality evaluation is published - the two examples are demonstrations, not measurements - and the author warns outputs can be incorrect or nonsensical. The licence is Google's Gemma terms (custom, not OSI-open), and the model is Turkish-only by design.
didnt: Rejected - licence (Gemma terms are ideas-only for us) and language scope; the extraction pattern (document in, typed nodes/edges JSON out, verify before trusting) parallels our claim-layer discipline, noted here without adoption. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: microsoft/tapex-base-finetuned-wikisql
good: A principled approach to table question answering from Microsoft Research: instead of pattern-matching cells, TAPEX pretrains a BART model as a neural SQL executor on a synthetic corpus of executable queries, then fine-tunes on WikiSQL - so its answers are computed by an internalised execution semantics rather than retrieved, the strongest idea in the table-QA line of its era.
bad: The card publishes no accuracy for this checkpoint and scopes it to 'relatively simple questions'; answers come back as bare values (1.0, 2008.0) with no query shown and no provenance - you cannot audit why an answer is what it is, which is the opposite of an evidence-carrying answer.
didnt: Rejected - a 2022 research checkpoint for table QA; recorded because table/image evidence evaluation is one of our open gaps, and TAPEX's executor-pretraining idea (learn to run the query, not to guess the cell) is the principled ancestor of the verifiable-table-answering we lack. The model itself is not adoptable into a prose-and-citation stack. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)
