good: A copilot that suggests — clear titles, single focused ideas, relevant links, tags, and how to split an over-full note — rather than rewriting unilaterally; batch embedding is scoped by explicit allow-patterns with the matched file list shown for verification before the run starts; unchanged notes are not re-embedded (content compared first), and similar-note results carry their cosine scores.
bad: Embeddings and copilot calls go to OpenAI/Anthropic APIs, so note content leaves the machine by design; indexing coverage is silent — unindexed notes simply never appear in results, with only a README note telling the user to run batch indexing; no answer or citation layer.
didnt: Corroboration: suggest-don't-rewrite copilot behaviour, verify-the-file-list-before-indexing and content-change-gated re-embedding all match our review-first discipline; the catalogue's ALREADY HAVE verdict is not repeated — no lane-8 record covers it. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: AI Notes Summary
good: Finds every link in the current note and generates a GPT summary of each linked note, presented together in a dialog; the plugin does not modify any note — the user copies the summary and pastes it where they choose. The prompt can be set per-note in frontmatter with a settings default, a shape aimed at weekly and monthly rollups of daily notes.
bad: GPT-3-era (created 2023) and requires an OpenAI API key; summaries arrive with no passage locators, citations or verification — an ungrounded digest the user must trust or re-check by hand.
didnt: Corroboration: a summariser that structurally cannot write — output lands only where the user pastes it — is our read-door posture in consumer form; nothing adopted, since our rollups are compiled pages carrying citations. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Notes Refresher
good: Summarises every Markdown note in a chosen folder, subfolders included, with GPT-4 and shows the results in a modal for review; folder path and regex matching are configurable, so a review pass can be scoped to one corner of a vault.
bad: Single-author with 1 star; OpenAI-only; summaries carry no source locators and the README documents no tests or evaluation of summary quality.
didnt: Rejected — duplication/scope: a generic folder summariser with no evidence machinery; our compiled summaries are pages with citations, not modal digests. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: AI Transcriber
good: Speech-to-text over OpenAI's GPT Transcribe / GPT-4o Transcribe / Whisper models with an exemplary disclosure set: a Network Usage Disclosure naming exactly what leaves the machine, a Local data and permissions section, bounded transcription history with full transcripts not retained as a second copy, API keys persisted only when OS safeStorage encryption is available, no telemetry, and a recovery window that shows the complete generated Markdown if creating the note fails.
bad: Audio is sent to OpenAI's paid API — custody of the recording leaves the machine by design; desktop only; the local-decode path caps at 128 MiB of encoded media and 2 hours of decoded audio.
didnt: Corroboration: the disclosure discipline — network use, local data, key storage and failure recovery all stated in the open — is the standard our own doors document themselves against; the transcription itself is not adopted (hosted-API custody of recordings, and our ingest works from text). (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Zotero Integration
good: The established Zotero-to-Obsidian bridge: insert citations and bibliographies, import notes and PDF annotations, driven by Better BibTeX citekeys, with 131 releases of maintenance behind it — the vault-side literature-note surface of the scholarly commons.
bad: GPL-3.0, so code is ideas only under the licence discipline; it requires the Better BibTeX plugin inside Zotero; its own README states the documentation is currently incomplete; nothing checks that an imported citation still resolves.
didnt: Corroboration: Zotero as the scholarly record our citation machinery presupposes, with the literature note as the compiled page on the vault side; GPL-3.0 code is ideas only. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Simple Citations
good: Literature notes are generated and updated in bulk from the bibliography file — add the item in Zotero and the note follows, optionally automatically when the bibliography changes; the notes double as the reference list for Pandoc citeproc export to docx with per-note citation styles. Its bulk property-removal command previews how many notes will be affected before the user confirms, and properties the plugin manages cannot be removed through it.
bad: Depends on Better BibTeX inside Zotero and on Pandoc for export; citekeys containing characters illegal in Obsidian filenames are skipped with only a console log; switching an optional field off removes that content from notes on the next update.
didnt: Corroboration: previewing the blast radius of a bulk edit before confirming, with protected fields the tool refuses to touch, is our approval-gated write discipline stated inside a citation tool; nothing adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: ZotLit
good: Turns Zotero items into templated Markdown literature notes with citation insertion, note import and an annotation sidebar, everything staying as plain Markdown in the vault. Its Disclosures section is unusually candid: it reads the Zotero database directly but never writes to it, live updates stay on localhost, the one shell command it invokes is named with its purpose, and users are told to back up before use.
bad: AGPL-3.0, so code is ideas only under the licence discipline; v2 is a breaking upgrade — existing literature notes and custom templates do not carry over unchanged; reading Zotero's database directly couples it to Zotero internals, which the README admits may break when Zotero updates.
didnt: Corroboration: read-only against the source database, with every side effect printed in a disclosures section, is the custody posture our ingest claims; AGPL code is ideas only. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Clipper
good: Captures highlights from the web as Markdown entries in the daily or weekly note through a bookmarklet, converting highlighted HTML tables to Markdown tables; a Network Use Notice discloses that the optional Chrome-extension wrapper is generated by an external service the author runs, rather than hiding the call.
bad: Highlight capture only — no page snapshot, source verification or dedup; the browser-extension path depends on the author's external service being up and trustworthy.
didnt: Corroboration: verbatim capture landing in the daily note is the ingest shape our conversation log uses, at web scale; nothing adopted — our ingest preserves the full source, not highlights alone. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Link Exploder
good: Builds an Obsidian canvas from a note that embeds its incoming and outgoing links plus their linked notes — a Map of Contents turned into a visual map of how topics interact, an interactive form of the local graph.
bad: The README calls it a first release, 'very basic at the moment'; it is presentation only — the canvas adds no content, evidence or structure to the notes themselves, and is dropped in the vault root.
didnt: Rejected — presentation-only: a rendering of a link graph we already traverse in text, with no knowledge function of its own. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Direct Git Sync
good: One-action vault-to-GitHub sync (stage, commit, fetch, merge, push) built on isomorphic-git, working on desktop and mobile with no Git installation. Conflicts never discard work: the local file stays in place and the remote version is saved as a separate conflict copy; a first sync creates local backups before anything is overwritten; a history modal shows the last successful sync and recent commit hashes.
bad: The GitHub personal access token is stored in a plugin data file inside the vault, protected only by the plugin ignoring its own data.json; its setup steps instruct a classic token with full repo scope and no expiration; created in March 2026 with 7 stars, it is unproven.
didnt: Corroboration: conflict copies instead of silent overwrite, and backup before first checkout, are our never-discard discipline in a sync tool; two-way multi-device sync itself stays outside the single-writer design, and the token-in-vault practice is recorded against it. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Fit
good: GitHub vault sync for mobile and desktop whose stated principles are conflict-safety: a both-sides-changed file keeps the local version in place and preserves the remote version side-by-side in a _fit/ folder for human resolution, while safe changes merge automatically; .obsidian/ configuration is excluded by default and only syncs by opt-in, so nothing sensitive travels by chance; an Explain Sync Status command reports pending changes, unresolved conflicts and files too large to push; fine-grained tokens need only Contents read/write.
bad: Still in beta by its own README, which asks users to back up first; if the same file clashes again before resolution, the earlier _fit/ conflict copy is overwritten by the latest remote version; GitHub API file-size limits (~100 MB hard, trouble above ~10 MB) bound what can sync.
didnt: Corroboration: conflicts preserved for a human rather than resolved silently, protected paths excluded by default, and sync state answerable on demand match our custody and status-from-record practices; not adopted — Obsidian is not our substrate and multi-device two-way sync is outside the design. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: AI Assistant
good: Chat and prompt modes against OpenAI and Anthropic models from inside a note; in prompt mode the user chooses whether generated text replaces the selection or is added below it, so the landing of a write is a user decision; Whisper dictation is inserted at the cursor.
bad: A generic model front-end: no retrieval over the vault, no citations or grounding for what it generates; everything runs through OpenAI/Anthropic API keys, so note content leaves for the provider on every use.
didnt: Rejected — duplication/scope: a chat surface with no evidence machinery; our Ask door answers from the corpus with citations and scored abstention instead. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: AI Chat Assistant
good: Multi-provider chat with a local-first knowledge base: hybrid search (vector similarity, keywords, recency) fused by RRF with graph-aware retrieval that follows note links, vectors held in IndexedDB, and a fully offline mode through Ollama; agent tools ask permission before changing anything. Its README's disclosure is exemplary — it states plainly that some features read and write outside the vault, that installing a skill is equivalent to running its code, that its built-in HTTP API has no authentication, and lists 'no automated tests' among its known limitations.
bad: Three commits and a personal project with no maintenance promise and, by its own account, no automated tests and unfinished large-file splits; the skill system executes installed code; MCP support is HTTP/SSE only and little exercised against real servers.
didnt: Corroboration: disclosure that names the dangerous surfaces instead of hiding them, and permission prompts ahead of agent writes, are our gateway posture independently arrived at; nothing adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: AI Commander
good: Generates text, images and transcripts from a prompt, a selection, the current line or the PDF embedded in the note; can ground generation in Bing search results; custom prompt commands can be registered from settings and reused from the palette.
bad: Its Prompt Perfect feature automatically replaces the user's own prompt with an 'improved' one before use; it needs OpenAI and Bing API keys; a 2023-era GPT-4 design with no retrieval over the vault and no citations.
didnt: Rejected — scope/duplication: a generation connector with no evidence machinery, and silent prompt-rewriting runs directly against our verbatim discipline. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: AI Organiser
good: A broad suite — summarisation, deck building, meeting minutes, semantic RAG across 14 providers plus local options — carrying two disciplines worth naming: every AI write shows an inline diff preview the user approves before it lands, and web research decomposes a question into sub-queries, scores source quality and answers with numbered citations (DOI extraction and author-year formatting in academic mode), with budget guardrails and cost shown and confirmed before paid narration calls.
bad: GPL-3.0, so code is ideas only under the licence discipline; a sprawling single-plugin scope; the newsletter feature reaches Gmail through an Apps Script bridge; 3 stars despite the feature count and a claimed 5,700+ tests.
didnt: Corroboration: diff-preview-before-landing is approval-gated writing in consumer form, and cost-confirmed-before-spend matches our money discipline; GPL-3.0 code is ideas only. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: AI Providers
good: A shared provider hub: API keys and model settings are configured once and consumed by other plugins through an SDK covering generation, tool calling, embeddings and local vector retrieval with an embedding cache. Model capabilities are explicit declarations — the README insists the checkboxes are declarations, not automatic detection, that a Check probes and preserves the manual set, and that support is never inferred from a model name; the cache's identity limits (a model changed behind an unchanged endpoint and name cannot be detected) are printed in the open.
bad: It centralises every consuming plugin's provider keys in one plugin's storage — a single point of compromise for the whole vault's AI access; shared embeddings across plugins remain roadmap rather than shipped.
didnt: Corroboration: capabilities declared and probed, never inferred from names, is the declaration discipline our own tool surfaces follow; the hub itself is not adopted — Obsidian plugin infrastructure is not our substrate. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Ayanite
licence: None stated (no LICENSE file in the repository; the README's Commercial section declares the plugin closed-source commercial software, free only for evaluation)
good: The storage shape is the right instinct: chats, prompts and profiles live as local Markdown files in the vault rather than in a vendor cloud, and messages go directly from the app to the user's chosen provider with zero telemetry claimed — the file-over-app half of our conversation-log practice, corroborated from the commercial side of the ecosystem (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: There is nothing to inspect: no source code in the repository at all, closed-source commercial terms, and paid-licence reminders for unlicensed users; the headline 'chat with your notes' capability is roadmap, not shipped (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Rejected — a closed-source shell repository with nothing auditable and a commercial licence gate; only its file-over-app chat storage corroborates a practice we already run. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Canvas LLM Extender
good: The interaction is genuinely small and legible: generation is anchored to the node's existing edge neighbourhood, so the model writes from the graph's own context rather than from nothing, and it runs against a local service as readily as against OpenAI (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: Self-declared alpha with unhandled errors and breakage on non-text nodes; more fundamentally the model writes new nodes straight into the canvas with no review step — generation lands as structure before a human has judged it (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Rejected — immature by its author's own account, and its unreviewed model-written nodes are the ungated-write pole our approval-gated writes exist against. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Caret
good: Corroboration: published design principles used as an admission gate for features, and conversation logs kept as Markdown files in the vault, are our own constitution-and-log practices stated independently — principles first, chats as files, local-first with providers as the only egress (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: Unmaintained by its author's own notice, so the corroboration is of the design, not of a living codebase; chat-with-vault generation carries the usual ungrounded-answer risk the principles do not address (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Corroboration — principles-as-gate and chat-logs-as-files corroborate the wiki's schema discipline and conversation log; nothing adopted from an unmaintained plugin. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Companion
good: Corroboration: acceptance is per word — nothing enters the note until the writer accepts that increment, so the human gate operates at the finest possible grain and the model can never land a paragraph unreviewed (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: The completions continue the writer's style, not the record's facts: ungrounded generation one accepted word at a time is still ungrounded, and fluent drift is hardest to notice exactly at this grain (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Corroboration — accept-per-increment is human-gated writing at keystroke grain and corroborates the approval discipline; the generation itself is style continuation, not evidence work, and is not adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Explain Selection With AI
good: Endpoint freedom is the one sound choice: any OpenAI-compatible backend, including a local Ollama, so the explanation need never leave the machine (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: A 13-commit first project with a single feature; the elaboration is ungrounded model prose about the selection with no source, no citation and no check — explanation-shaped text is precisely what a corpus must not absorb as knowledge (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Rejected — scope and maturity: a single-feature elaboration toy whose output has no grounding machinery at all. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Study generators (grouped: Flashcards LLM, Quiz Generator, LLM Test Generator)
good: The mechanics are tidy: generation is scoped to a selection or a named note, lands in a delimited blockquote rather than overwriting prose, carries a tag for the spaced-repetition pipeline, and exposes an explicit token budget (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: The cards are unverified model output appended straight into the note — wrong facts become study material with no correctness check anywhere in the pipeline, and the README's own formatting caveats show the failure is routine, not rare (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Rejected — generated study artefacts enter the corpus unchecked; the homeschool corpus verifies content before it is taught, which is the opposite pipeline. Judged on the grouped entry's named repository, whose pattern the group shares. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Hints Flow
licence: CC BY-NC 4.0 (LICENSE.md carries the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International text; GitHub licence detection reads Other (NOASSERTION))
good: The separation it draws is clean: capture channel, flow logic and note template are distinct layers, and almost any messaging surface can feed one vault endpoint through a user-built template (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: Custody: captured message content transits the vendor's hosted service and account before it reaches the vault — the vault receives what a third party already holds; the licence is also non-commercial Creative Commons, ideas-only under our discipline regardless (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Rejected — a hosted capture intermediary holding the content upstream of the vault; our ingest runs under our own custody end to end. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: LLM Translate
good: Corroboration: three write-safety disciplines in one small plugin — a never-touch region (frontmatter is neither sent nor edited), cancel-restores-original (an aborted operation leaves the note exactly as it was), and a size threshold that forces a confirmation before a large send (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: Brand new and tiny (10 commits, 1 star); in replace mode the original survives only through the cancel/undo path, and translation quality itself is unexamined model output (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Corroboration — frontmatter preservation, full-restore cancellation and the long-note confirmation corroborate the write-discipline family our tools already practise; translation itself is out of scope. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Pocket Sync
good: Corroboration: the managed block is the machine-region/user-region boundary again — synced content owns a delimited region of the note and the human's surrounding writing is never overwritten — and the raw transcript is imported as its own note beside the derived summary and action items, source and derivative kept apart (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: Ten commits and brand new; the upstream Pocket AI service holds the recordings and produces the transcripts and summaries, so the vault sync is only as trustworthy as that vendor pipeline (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Corroboration — managed-block sync regions and transcript-beside-summary separation corroborate our raw/compiled split; the vendor-dependent upstream is recorded, not adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Mindmap AI
good: Corroboration, several disciplines at once: consent-gated egress that starts manual, derived queries instead of raw notes leaving the machine, secrets in the OS keychain, redacted diagnostics, a read-only posture toward the source database, and a staged index swap that activates only after verification — the same shape as our verify-before-replace discipline (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: One star and weeks old despite the polish; generated summaries, tags and concepts are written into note properties automatically, so model judgements accumulate in the corpus metadata without a review step; several features are macOS-bound (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Corroboration — consent-first egress, staged-and-verified index migration and diagnostics redaction corroborate standing disciplines; the automatic property-writing is recorded against it and nothing is adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: MoreDraw
good: The disclosure itself is at least upfront: the README's first note tells the user the drawing surface is a remote service with accounts and paid tiers before they install, rather than letting them discover it (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: The plugin is a shell: the whiteboard, saving and sync live on the vendor's remote service, so vault-adjacent work product sits in a third party's custody behind a freemium gate (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Rejected — a remote-service whiteboard wrapped as a plugin; hosted custody of the artefact is the disqualifier, as with the other service shells in this wave. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Personal Assistant
good: Corroboration: the per-feature egress table (trigger / data sent / destination / background / user control) is the most complete disclosure surface in this wave and a template for how a gateway should account for itself; keeping the derived index out of the vault, asking before costly rebuilds, and discovery-that-never-writes corroborate three more standing disciplines (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: AGPL-3.0 keeps it ideas-only regardless; and the first-use background Memory preparation can spend API credits before any explicit ask — disclosed, but still a spend-first default that sits against our ask-before-costly-work rule (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Corroboration — its egress accounting, index-out-of-vault choice and ask-before-costly-work prompts corroborate the gateway's disclosure and custody disciplines; AGPL makes it a study, never a source. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Shell Path Copy
good: Corroboration: a tool that names its single write case in one sentence and makes everything else read-only is the disclosure shape we ask of our own doors; its line-reference format (file.md#L42) is the same path-plus-line addressing our wiki citations use (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: It is a clipboard utility — no knowledge machinery to adopt; and even its one write is a side effect of a copy action, a marker landing in a note because the user asked for a link (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Corroboration — the one-write-case disclosure and line-addressed references corroborate citation and door discipline; the utility itself is out of scope. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: YouTube summarizers (grouped: YouTube Video Summarizer, YTSummarizer)
good: The pipeline starts from the right material — the actual transcript — and marks its own failure mode inside the artefact: a truncated summary says so in the note itself, and per-model pricing is shown before the user spends (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: The transcript itself is not kept: the note holds only the model's summary and metadata, so nothing in the corpus lets a reader check the summary's claims against what was actually said — the derivative survives and the source is discarded (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Rejected — a summary without its transcript is unverifiable in-corpus; our ingest keeps the raw source beside the compiled page precisely so derivations stay checkable. Judged on the grouped entry's named repository. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Agent Skill Graph
good: Corroboration: a strictly read-only, in-memory overlay that makes an agent's capability structure — which agent can see which skills, which references leave the vault — visible without touching a single file is our read-door philosophy drawn as a graph; unresolved references shown as explicit virtual nodes, never silently dropped or invented, is the honest-gap shape our door records use (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: It works by patching undocumented Obsidian internals (PixiJS renderer text, metadataCache link tables), which is brittle across Obsidian versions; and clicking an external virtual node creates a blank note instead of opening the source — a small trap in an otherwise careful design (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Corroboration — read-only visualisation of agent↔skill structure with honest virtual nodes corroborates the door and gap-record disciplines; the undocumented-API brittleness is recorded and nothing is adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Agentfiles
good: Corroboration: explicit-action-only writes, SHA-pinned installs with traversal rejection and size caps, no process spawning, and a risk capability disclosed in the open with its justification — the permission-accounting shape our own doors are held to (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: Its conversation browsing and export is a session-transcript substrate — transcript ingest is unapproved in our system, so that feature is characterised, never taken; and a manager that can edit every agent's skill and memory files concentrates a great deal of write authority in one plugin (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Corroboration — the write-permission and install-pinning disciplines corroborate the gateway's accounting; the transcript-export feature is recorded as a substrate we do not use. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: EngramQuest
licence: Custom 'Engram Quest Plugin License' v1.0 (root LICENSE file: personal/internal use and redistribution with the licence, a non-compete clause barring derivative competing plugins, no sale of the software; GitHub licence detection reads Other (NOASSERTION))
good: Corroboration: generated material is quarantined in its own folder away from source notes, learner progress is stored apart from generated content so regeneration cannot destroy it, and course generation is outline-first with the plan approved before the expensive step — three separations our raw/compiled and approval disciplines share (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: The study material itself is AI-generated and unverified — the B156 flashcard problem in a larger frame; the licence is a custom non-compete, ideas-only under our discipline; and the paste-a-prompt onboarding hands an agent a standing instruction set at install time (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Corroboration — its quarantine, progress-separation and outline-approval shapes corroborate standing disciplines; the generated content and the custom licence keep it a study, never a source. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Lovely-Mindmap
good: The interaction design is thoughtful: a Creation view that deliberately makes focus hard to break, and full keyboard operation for users who never want to leave the keys (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: It is a drawing surface only — nothing here touches knowledge, evidence or memory; and a project that asks users not to file bug reports has opted out of the feedback loop a tool we relied on would need (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Rejected — presentation/editor scope, the same ground as the other canvas and rendering plugins in this wave. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: 3D Semantic Graph
good: Corroboration: a provider that cannot serve is shown disabled with its reason rather than silently substituted — no silent rerouting of note content — and externally supplied vectors are validated before they are trusted; both are small, exact instances of the honesty disciplines our retrieval work is judged by (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: The product is visualisation: embedding proximity rendered as space, with the generation path OpenAI-only; suggested links are similarity judgements, not evidence, and a 3D view answers no question our corpus asks (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Corroboration — the no-silent-rerouting and validate-before-accept details corroborate; the 3D presentation itself is out of scope. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Pretty BibTeX
good: Readable bibliography entries are genuinely nicer to proof-read, and the change is render-only: the underlying BibTeX text is never rewritten (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: Presentation only — no citation is resolved, verified or even parsed into fields, so it contributes nothing to the scholarly machinery (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Rejected — a rendering nicety, the same ground as B155's Link Exploder and B154's Frontmatter to HTML Attributes. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Stratum
good: Corroboration: the write-above-the-notice rule is the managed-region boundary stated as a user instruction — synced content owns its region and the human's writing above it is preserved by construction; retraction flags arriving with imported sources corroborate the truth-checking shelf (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: Account-gated with cloud imports through the vendor's service, so the scholarly corpus transits a third party on its way into the vault; the destination of the whole flow is a published paper, which for the private wiki is an owner-gated act, not a plugin feature (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Corroboration — region preservation and retraction-flag enrichment corroborate; the account and cloud-import custody are recorded, not adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Cockpit Board
good: Corroboration: a token scoped write-only to one topic because its storage file travels with the vault, and external-origin content forced through a warning dialog before an agent runs on it, are exactly the credential and untrusted-content disciplines our connectors and doors follow (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: The board itself is task management, out of scope; and a launcher that starts agents on machines over SSH from inside a notes plugin is a powerful surface even with its gates — the gates are the corroboration, not an adoption case (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Corroboration — its token scoping and external-content warning corroborate gate hygiene; the board and the launcher are not adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: GitHub Gitless Sync
good: Human-resolution-by-default conflicts and a single-repo fine-grained token are the right defaults for vault sync, stated and implemented at source (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: AGPL-3.0 makes it ideas-only regardless; it is GitHub-only by design — the catalogue's own note stands: our wiki's remote is Azure — and its metadata-file coupling makes it the sole permitted sync path or a data-loss risk (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Rejected — AGPL and a GitHub-only custody path; its conflict and token defaults are credited in the row, not adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Multi Cloud Sync
good: Dry-run-before-apply and a confirmation step are the right shape for any sync that can delete, and the corruption warnings are at least printed where a user will see them before enabling the experimental path (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: Vault folders come to live across third-party clouds — the custody the catalogue flagged — with the source itself warning of corruption and deletion on one provider, a paid tier holding the safer-looking features, and GPL-3.0 over the whole (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Rejected — multi-cloud custody of vault content, confirmed by the source's own data-loss warnings; its dry-run discipline is credited, not adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Publish and GitHub URL
good: Honouring `publish: false` — a note that says do-not-publish gets no publish affordance at all — is the right respect for a per-note boundary marker (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: The tool exists to serve public Publish sites; the private wiki is never published, so the surface it streamlines is one we deliberately do not have (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Rejected — a publishing-surface utility; only its respect for the publish flag is credited. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Ghost Writer Manager
good: Keychain-held credentials and a per-note opt-out flag are the right micro-disciplines for any outbound sync: the secret never sits in the vault as text, and the boundary can be declared on the note itself (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: Its purpose is a public publishing pipeline — notes flow to a public CMS automatically on save once enabled; public exposure of wiki material is an owner-gated act, and an always-on publish timer is the opposite posture from our read-only public stance (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Rejected — a public-publishing sync; its keychain storage and per-note opt-out are credited in the row. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Companion MCP
good: Corroboration: the read side is our door's shape independently built — local embeddings, line-anchored windowed reads, and read results that carry their own edit handoff instead of making the agent reconstruct anchors (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: The write side is ungated: edit, create, move and delete tools with no approval step, no read-only mode and no audit described anywhere in the README — a full-authority door, and its degraded mode keeps that authority when the app is closed (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Corroboration — the read/handoff design corroborates our read door; the ungated write surface is recorded as the contrast case, and nothing is adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: HangarX
good: Cited answers and source-tagged recall (memory vs graph kept distinguishable in the result) are the right retrieval manners, and a fully local Docker mode exists for users who refuse the cloud (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: In hosted mode the vault's graph — entities, relationships, embeddings — lives in the vendor's custody; in both modes the model is many agents writing one shared memory with automatic merges, the multi-writer design our wiki rejects by design; and baking provider keys into a file inside the vault is a credential-custody fault, stated in its own setup text (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Rejected — vendor-custodied or multi-writer shared memory, with keys written into the vault in local mode; its citation and source-tagging manners are credited in the row. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Agentic Note References
good: Corroboration: file-plus-line-range as the unit of a citation handed to an agent — with the referenced text travelling with the address — is our own ^[cite: path#Lx-Ly] practice reduced to a clipboard tool; an agent given lines 3–7 can check them, an agent given a note title cannot (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: AGPL-3.0 keeps it ideas-only; it is also tiny and new (29 commits, 1 star), and its Reading-mode preset quietly drops the line precision that is the tool's whole point (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Corroboration — line-addressed citation handoff corroborates the citation discipline; AGPL makes it a study, never a source. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: AI Attachmate
good: Corroboration: a transcript with a preserved user zone — generated content may be regenerated freely, the human's notes on it may not be touched — plus user-set scope, prompt and destination, is the managed-region discipline applied to OCR output, beside B154's HandTranscriptMd (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
bad: AGPL-3.0, ideas only; PDFs and images leave for Google Gemini (the only provider), and the inherited orphan-cleanup coupling deletes the derived transcript with its source — deletion by association, where our practice keeps the raw and the derived independently (completion pass, 2026-10-21).
didnt: Corroboration — user-zone preservation and user-controlled transcription scope corroborate; AGPL, single-vendor egress and delete-with-source coupling are recorded against it. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Briefmaker
good: Renders an AI-agent brief from the current note and copies it to the clipboard — it calls no APIs, runs no AI and modifies no notes. Path-based regex template rules (first match wins), unchecked-task extraction with indentation preserved, frontmatter/selection/file metadata as template variables, and a preview modal before anything is copied.
bad: Embryonic (14 commits, 1 star, created 2026-01-05). Brief quality rests entirely on user-written templates, and the shipped default template instructs the receiving agent to update a 'Tasks' file afterwards — an agent-addressed default carried inside the brief itself.
didnt: Corroboration — the clipboard-only handoff: the tool prepares context and a human carries it to the agent; nothing is written or sent by the tool itself. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Perplexed
good: Generates source-cited research content into notes from five provider routes (Perplexity, Claude, Gemini with search grounding, self-hosted Perplexica/Vane, local LM Studio). An Exa retrieval layer fetches sources before generation and splices them in under a separate citation namespace; a printed Network use and accounts table lists every endpoint, account and key requirement, and states nothing is sent automatically and no telemetry is collected.
bad: The citations are the provider's own — generated content lands in notes with no verification or locking against the source. The main providers are paid hosted APIs, so prompts and selected note content leave the machine by design; the README's centre of gravity is VC/PE analyst-template marketing.
didnt: Corroboration — retrieval-before-generation with a separate citation namespace for retrieved sources, and a full egress table as the disclosure surface. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Simple Graph Builder
good: Builds a lightweight knowledge graph (10 fixed entity types, free-form relationship verbs) with schema-enforced extraction — malformed entities are reported and dropped, never silently admitted. A hybrid entity-resolution pipeline reserves LLM verification for the genuinely ambiguous band; relationships keep verbatim quotes as evidence; agents query vault and graph through a local, token-protected, read-only MCP server; imported pages the user edited are never overwritten without their say-so; advanced search explains every result and makes no API calls.
bad: Extraction sends note content to cloud LLMs by default (per-token API costs are tabulated in its own README) and the graph is model-derived, never locked to source text. Opt-in vault write-back mirrors the derived graph into the notes themselves.
didnt: Corroboration — a read-only agent door over a derived graph, schema-validated admission, and never-overwrite import discipline. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Smart Linker
good: Finds semantically related notes from pre-computed local embeddings and writes them only inside a managed block (auto-related start/end markers) at the note's end — the rest of the note is never touched. Deduplicates chunked-embedding matches; threshold, top-K and folder exclusions are configurable.
bad: It computes nothing itself — it is wholly dependent on another plugin's embeddings file being present and current. Links land inside the block unreviewed (block-confined, but unreviewed); a tiny project (15 commits, 2 stars).
didnt: Corroboration — the managed-region write rule at plugin scale: an automated writer confined to its own marked block. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Semantic Linker
good: Indexes only note metadata (titles, filenames, tags, descriptions, type) — explicitly not full note bodies — and a printed Network use and privacy section states the only network calls go to the user-configured embedding provider, carrying metadata text, with no telemetry. Links are inserted only when the user clicks a candidate node; feedback-aware ranking ships off by default, with the sample-bias reason stated.
bad: Embryonic (6 commits, 1 star, created 2026-05-17). Recommendation quality collapses to frontmatter quality, and API keys are stored in the plugin's data.json — vault-resident plugin data, the storage location whose risk B157's Cockpit Board row records.
didnt: Corroboration — metadata-only egress with a privacy section as the disclosure surface, and human-click insertion. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: QMD Semantic Search
good: Fully local semantic search over the vault — no API keys, no cloud services, no remote LLM; the plugin drives the QMD CLI's semantic and keyword modes on the user's own machine. Semantic-first with a graceful BM25 fallback that shows a notice when the fallback was used; relevance scores displayed; index and embeddings maintained in the background.
bad: The plugin is a shell over an external CLI stack (Bun plus QMD plus a ~300 MB model download), so its quality and failure modes are the engine's, not its own. Young (18 commits); retrieval only, with no citation, abstention or conflict machinery.
didnt: Corroboration — local-first retrieval as commodity, with the degraded path (keyword fallback) labelled in the interface rather than silent. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Press PDF Export
good: Converts Obsidian Markdown to Pandoc Markdown and exports PDF, Word or HTML through local engines (XeLaTeX, wkhtmltopdf, WeasyPrint, Typst), with a content-fidelity table mapping Obsidian syntax — callouts, wikilinks, embeds, Mermaid pre-rendered to SVG — to its exported form. Batch export of a folder or the whole vault with concurrency control and skip-on-error.
bad: Five commits and one release — embryonic. Desktop-only and wholly dependent on a heavy local toolchain (Pandoc plus a TeX or HTML engine); an export formatter with no knowledge function.
didnt: Rejected — scope: presentation export only; our own PDF delivery already runs the WeasyPrint route directly. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Remote Vault Sync
good: Backs the vault up to the user's own S3 bucket with real git version control — the .git directory itself is mirrored, large files ride Git LFS, and diff, log and merge-conflict modals live inside Obsidian.
bad: The AWS access key and secret are entered into plugin settings — vault-adjacent credential storage. Restore discards local changes, and two devices merging one .git through S3 is the multi-writer shape our design rejects; embryonic (31 commits, 1 star).
didnt: Rejected — custody shape: the whole repository history sits in a bucket under plugin-held AWS credentials; our wiki's remote is Azure git with scoped, verified pushes. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Frontmatter boards (grouped: Base Board, Notion Bases, Kanban Sync)
good: Judged on the named repo (Base Board): 'Data First — all changes are written directly to your Markdown files.' The board is a view over frontmatter properties; dragging a card rewrites the property in the note itself and card order lives in a kanban_order property, not in a plugin database. Per-column WIP limits; a migration command lists legacy views, pre-selects the ones carrying its settings, and rewrites only the ones the user confirms.
bad: A task-board presentation layer with no knowledge, citation or evidence function. Board interaction writes metadata into every participating note's frontmatter, so the view's convenience is paid for in the record itself.
didnt: Corroboration — files-as-truth for derived views: the view holds no state of its own; the notes remain the record. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Simple exporter for LLM
good: Packages hand-picked folders, tags or files to the clipboard as structured XML/JSON with the folder and tag trees included and per-item path and created/modified stamps. A Context Builder lets the user remove individual files before copying, and tag filtering excludes notes by tag — including #private-style and nested tags — from every export.
bad: The README states the plugin is '100% generated using AI (Gemini CLI)'. Beyond the tag filter there is no redaction or review of what a whole-folder copy carries, and the project is tiny (15 commits, 3 stars).
didnt: Corroboration — exclusion-tag discipline plus a clipboard-only, human-carried handoff, the Briefmaker shape in the same batch. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Embed Metadata
good: Renders frontmatter values inline in reading view via [%key] / {{key}} markers, including cross-note [%[[Note]]@property] references. A missing key, note or property leaves the marker unchanged — fail-visible, nothing invented — and its vault-wide migrations open a review modal listing matching files with counts, letting the user deselect files before any edit lands.
bad: Presentation only — a Dataview inline-field replacement with no knowledge, search or evidence function. Rendered values are resolved relative to the target note, so a reader sees a value whose home is another page.
didnt: Rejected — scope: rendering only; its review-modal-before-vault-wide-edit gate is credited in good. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Engram Vault Sync
good: 'Nothing is ever silently overwritten'; the first sync sends nothing until the user confirms. A Privacy section states the plugin talks only to the user's Engram server, with no telemetry and optional remote logging off by default; keyword search works locally and offline; a self-host route exists (backend described as source-available).
bad: The default route is the vendor's hosted cloud holding the whole vault, and the MCP surface lets any connected AI read and write notes with no approval gating described. API keys on the hosted tier are Pro-gated.
didnt: Rejected — hosted custody by default plus an ungated multi-client write surface. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Mengram
good: Folder include/exclude filtering controls what syncs, and a printed Network usage section states plainly that note content is sent to the Mengram API for extraction and storage, and that nothing is sent without an API key configured. A self-host base-URL option exists.
bad: Auto-sync on save (2-second debounce, on by default) streams note content to the vendor cloud, where entities and facts are extracted server-side as a black box — the inverse of approval-gated ingest. The free tier is metered (100 adds/month).
didnt: Rejected — hosted custody with automatic egress on every save. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Superpower Inside
good: Citations point to a path, heading, line or PDF page, and the source panel shows checked passages, sources needing review, and material left out by processing limits — omissions are surfaced, not hidden. A document that exceeds budget or cannot be read completely errors and its partial text is not used. Credentials live in Obsidian's secret storage, explicitly separate from vault-synced plugin settings; local search and on-device OCR; an exclusion property keeps notes out.
bad: Remote chat and remote embeddings send selected material to the chosen provider, and the README itself concedes search does not read the whole vault and a checked passage does not guarantee a correct answer. 'The only AI option for Obsidian Vault' marketing over a 4-star project.
didnt: Corroboration — an omission-surfacing work log, fail-closed partial reads, and secret storage separated from synced settings. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Similarity
good: Fully on-device semantic search and related-note exploration: no internet required after install, no API keys, no tracking or telemetry, and its printed Priorities refuse any feature that would violate locality, even as an opt-in. Bug reports go through the user's own browser or mail client with the full content shown to the user first. The batch's most mature plugin (327 commits, since 2024-10-31).
bad: Retrieval only — relatedness with no citations, provenance or write discipline. The README presents features as images and documents no mechanism or evaluation.
didnt: Corroboration — local-only custody held as an inviolable design constraint rather than a setting. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Graphene
good: Similarity edges are drawn dotted and kept distinct from explicit links, so inferred connections never masquerade as drawn ones; a local Ollama embedding path is the recommended default; incremental embedding updates process only changed files; template-similarity guards (skip initial words, exclude headings) are built in; a test suite ships in the repo.
bad: The OpenAI option sends note content to a cloud embedder; the plugin is not yet in the Obsidian directory (manual install only) and began as a hack-event prototype; GPL-3.0 puts the code in the ideas-only class under our licence discipline regardless.
didnt: Rejected (licence: GPL-3.0 — ideas only, no code taken): the display discipline it embodies — inferred edges visually distinct from explicit links, incremental embeddings, template-similarity guards — corroborates our own link-provenance practice, and nothing here needs building. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Graph Mind
type: Obsidian plugin (local vault chat and search)
good: Fully local by construction — the only network peer is the user's own Ollama; citations are numbered links into the source notes; an advanced filter syntax (phrases, tags, paths, exclusions) sharpens retrieval; the README's Privacy section and its honest no-Ollama degradation are printed plainly; third-party licences are itemised in the README.
bad: Very young and small (16 commits, 3 stars); no abstention or conflict behaviour is described for questions the vault cannot answer; GPL-3.0 puts the code in the ideas-only class under our licence discipline.
didnt: Rejected (licence: GPL-3.0 — ideas only, no code taken): as a pattern it corroborates local-only cited chat over a vault, which our Ask door already implements with abstention and conflict gates this plugin does not describe. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: ZotFlow
good: The conflict model is the careful one: per-library sync direction, field-level merge, and a diff viewer that leaves genuinely contested fields to the human; credentials live in native secret storage, explicitly never in the synced settings file; offline-first with no telemetry; sync is tested against fixtures with fault injection, a testing depth rare in this wave.
bad: AGPL-3.0 puts the code in the ideas-only class under our licence discipline; the whole design orbits a Zotero library, which is not our citation substrate (ours is file-level sources); in bidirectional mode, child-note edits auto-save and sync back without a review step.
didnt: Rejected (licence: AGPL-3.0 — ideas only, no code taken): its sync-conflict discipline and credential storage corroborate our own custody rules, and the Zotero-centred shape does not fit our file-level citation system. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Make It Rain
good: The Safe Sync rule — an uncertain answer is never treated as a deletion, ambiguity is bucketed and forced to manual review — is exactly the discipline our door records apply to uncertain sources; per-item ignore/archive/delete choice with a configurable trash folder; templates, AND/OR tag filtering and selective new-only imports make the import reviewable; token verification is a distinct step before first import.
bad: The source of truth is a Raindrop.io cloud account, a service we do not use; the API token is pasted into plugin settings with no secret-storage statement; the Safe Sync default action can be set to Delete, weakening its own safeguard by configuration.
didnt: Corroboration: its confirmed-deletion-only rule corroborates our uncertain-answer handling (a maybe is never a deletion, in sync or in research); the importer itself serves a bookmark service outside our system, so nothing is adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: JotDrop
type: Obsidian plugin + Android app + Chrome clipper (quick capture)
good: Capture discipline is right: offline, account-free, plain Markdown in the user's own vault; refcount-aware deletion protects shared attachments; the never-lose-a-clip fallback and the sync-conflict handshake show failure-first design; the signing-key candour ('not proof of authenticity') is the honest way to ship a sideloaded APK.
bad: Three components (plugin, Android app, extension) is a wide surface for a capture tool; Android OCR's ML Kit SDK 'sends technical diagnostics to Google' by the README's own privacy note; a known issue around bulk delete while a sync peer is offline is still open; the project is months old and its Play-test machinery dominates the README.
didnt: Corroboration: its capture rules — plain files, refcount-aware delete, fallback so nothing captured is lost — corroborate our ingest discipline; quick capture is not a gap in our system, so nothing is adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Handwriting to Text
good: The transcription is reviewed and editable before anything is inserted — the human gate sits in the right place for OCR; the Privacy section is short and honest about where images go; HEIC handling and multilingual transcription are covered; the prompt is customisable per handwriting style.
bad: Handwriting images leave the device to Google's API by design; the API key sits in the vault-resident plugin data folder, so it travels with any vault sync; the project is tiny (10 commits, 0 stars) and lists preview-tier models as supported.
didnt: Corroboration: the review-and-edit-before-insert gate corroborates our OCR posture (our OCR queue is human-verified before text enters the wiki); cloud-only recognition and vault-resident keys are the standing pattern we do not adopt. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Tegaki
type: Obsidian plugin (handwriting OCR with annotation position)
good: Position-aware extraction is genuinely distinctive: an annotation's meaning often is its placement, and this records placement as data; a handwriting-only command separates annotation from print; the sensitive-content warning is printed before setup, not buried; supported formats and the vault-image behaviour are explained plainly.
bad: Images go to external vision APIs by design; the key lives in vault data.json; at 7 commits and 1 star the project is embryonic, with region-ordered OCR still on the roadmap.
didnt: Corroboration: position-context extraction for annotations is an OCR idea our human-verified queue could borrow in principle, and its upfront sensitive-image warning is the right pattern; the product itself is embryonic and cloud-bound, so nothing is adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Git sync variants (grouped: Easy Git, Git Folder Sync, magneto, Vault Sync (REST))
type: Obsidian plugins (git/GitHub vault sync) — grouped entry, judged on Easy Git
good: Easy Git's fail-safes are the careful kind: a missing folder aborts rather than deletes, credentials sit in the OS keychain per device, transforms are push-side-only with a lossless round-trip, and one destination's failure does not poison the others; folder-scoped direction control matches how a governed vault would ever sync; a SECURITY.md ships at root.
bad: The classic-token route asks for broad repo scope; in pull multi-destination mappings, same-named files overwrite last-writer-wins by stated design; timer- and on-save-triggered sync is standing automation over vault history, which our governed, deliberate-commit custody does not run; the other three grouped members were not opened and inherit no judgement from this row.
didnt: Corroboration: folder-scoped sync with fail-safe aborts and keychain custody is the right shape for any future vault-sync question; live sync automation itself stays unbuilt under our deliberate-commit custody. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Agentic Git Sync
good: When the agent cannot decide a conflict, it shows its suggestion, its confidence and its reasoning side by side rather than hiding the choice; AI-drafted commit messages remain editable before commit; the GitHub App credential route (repo-scoped, short-lived, revocable) and the schema-level guarantee that no token can be committed are well judged.
bad: The default path is autonomous custody of history: automatic merges, invisible background push/pull, silent initial commits — the owner never sees most operations on their own record; AI-drafted messages blur authorship of the history they describe; a PAT fallback lives in local data.json.
didnt: Rejected: autonomous git custody — auto-merging branches and background sync over the vault's history is precisely the autonomy our governed custody refuses, whatever the resolver's confidence display; the confidence-rated three-pane resolver and the no-token-in-config schema are the salvageable ideas. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: AI Wiki
good: The ingest mechanics are disciplined: guarded section patches instead of page rewrites, bounded chunks with complete evidence coverage, tag-vocabulary reuse with bounded categories; the Format invariant (clarity only, never facts) with a preview; the directory disclosures are a model of plain dealing; ambiguous release state halts publication rather than guessing.
bad: The wiki itself is written and 'fixed' by the model on a chat instruction, with no owner-approval gate over content — the exact failure our propose-then-approve writes exist to prevent; Re-init deletes and recreates the whole domain tree as a routine operation; 2,479 commits against 5 stars marks machine-paced development whose volume is not evidence of judgement; its OKF type system is Google's schema, not ours.
didnt: Corroboration: its ingest mechanics corroborate our ingest design at plugin scale (guarded patches, complete-evidence chunking, vocabulary discipline); the auto-maintained, model-written wiki is the pattern our approval gates govern, so the product is not adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Local LLM Hub

name: Vault Curate
type: Obsidian plugin (local-first semantic search and rediscovery)

(completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Synod
type: Obsidian plugin (LLM value-council over a journal)

bad: Nine commits and zero stars: a sketch, not a system; scheduled automatic runs over a personal journal are background processing of the most private text a vault holds; the premise refuses compromise on principle — surfacing tensions is useful, but a decisions system that will not resolve them is a stance, not a tool; journal records sit in data.json.
didnt: Corroboration: its three-pass compiler (evidence gate before any claim is written) corroborates our gate-before-write design in miniature; the journaling product itself is not adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: IStart-Note-AI
type: Obsidian plugin (DeepSeek knowledge and writing suite)

name: Zotero Research Assistant
type: Obsidian plugin (Zotero PDF RAG over local Redis)

name: Git File Sync

name: Claude Skill Sync

name: EVC Local Sync to AI Agent

name: Granola Meetings Simple Sync

name: LinkVault
type: Obsidian plugin (AI link filing into a knowledge base)
good: The routing honesty is the point: duplicates are reported with their location instead of silently refiled, and a misfit becomes a new note instead of a wrong home; the auto-generated index never edits curated notes; keys live in the platform secret store; raw model responses are inspectable in debug mode.

name: Custom Publish

name: Canvas gadgets (grouped: Detailed Canvas, Canvas Banana, Overboard, Icon Board, Mermaid Base Views)

name: Cite
good: Duplicate keys get a deterministic rule AND disclosure, instead of silent first-found behaviour; bounded scanning by configuration; parser non-goals stated as design, so users are not surprised by silent partial parses.
bad: Pandoc locators, prefixes, suffixes and suppressed-author forms are unsupported in this release; 18 commits and 1 star; trilingual UI breadth at this size spreads effort thin.
didnt: Corroboration: deterministic, disclosed conflict resolution and printed parser limits corroborate our citation and fail-visible discipline; nothing is adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: OneBib
good: Scope modesty printed in the README rather than discovered by users; minimal-access import (only the file the user picks); the marker-stays-in-source design keeps notes portable if the plugin vanishes.
bad: One APA-like style only so far; the imported .bib is copied to the vault root, which both clutters and creates a second source of truth against the original file; 6 commits and 0 stars.
didnt: Corroboration: another managed-block citation face with honest scope; our citation machinery is file-level with its own marker discipline, so nothing is adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Ambient Backlinks
type: Obsidian plugin (LLM explanations of backlink relationships)
good: It explains the connection, not the content — typed edges are what a link graph actually needs; egress is minimised to the linking paragraph, not whole notes; failure leaves a visible 'not explained' state instead of a fabricated line.
bad: The relationship line is model-generated and unverified — a fluent, wrong edge label ('contradicts') is worse than no label, and nothing in the design checks it; Auto mode fires on navigation; 6 commits and 0 stars.
didnt: Corroboration: typed link relationships with a visible unexplained state corroborate our link-semantics interests; the unverified-label risk is recorded against any quiet adoption, and nothing is taken. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Smart Notes
type: Obsidian plugin (AI workspace: chat, skills, profile memory)
good: On-demand search with caps beats load-the-whole-vault context assembly; optimisation is previewed as a diff, not applied blind; secret-storage key custody; search providers and egress triggers are itemised in the Privacy section.
bad: Background distillation of conversations into an auto-injected profile is automatic memory-writing — the pattern our system deliberately keeps human-gated, deliberate and filed (its MEMORY.md is a namesake of our own memory file, a different system; identity kept separate here); skill packages can be uploaded as zips from skill hubs and loaded at the AI's request (@use-skill), a supply-chain surface; the feature surface is enormous for 143 commits.
didnt: Corroboration: on-demand bounded search and diff-before-apply corroborate our context and write disciplines; the background auto-profile is recorded as the contrast case to our compiled, visible memory — nothing is adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Colloquy
good: The most honest README in this batch: surprising behaviour is disclosed before installation, not under Advanced; removing a feature for producing confident false claims — and publishing the ADR — is exactly the correction culture our own ledger keeps; cost-bearing automation is designed out, not warned about.
bad: API keys are stored in the plugin's own data file — never rendered back, but plaintext-at-rest class custody; the auto-account still writes without per-write approval (disclosed and disable-able, but on by design); 48 commits and 0 stars.
didnt: Corroboration: agent-marked, hint-not-fact accounts and a decision log that keeps reversed decisions corroborate our ingest-honesty rules directly; conversation-transcript ingest itself remains unapproved in our system, so the tool is not adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Local Agent Assistant
type: Obsidian plugin (local agent CLI bridge with evidence citations)
good: Evidence-linked answers with navigable citations are the right default for agent-over-vault work; review items are addressable objects (REV-NNN) rather than prose; shell-free process invocation is stated and deliberate.
bad: A single commit — no development provenance at all; the read-only default is a request in the prompt, not a capability boundary: an agent that ignores the instruction faces no enforcement, the gap between asking and enforcing; 'bounded' evidence is never quantified.
didnt: Corroboration: bounded evidence, path#section citations and shell-free invocation corroborate our door habits; the prompt-level read-only is recorded as weaker than our capability-level read-only door, and nothing is adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Soma Search
type: Obsidian plugin (local multimodal search front end)
good: Disclosure quality is exemplary — plaintext index, uninstall residue, symlink-following and memory hunger are all printed where users will see them before installing; loopback-only transport; results open Markdown at the matching line.
bad: A plaintext full-text index of the whole vault sitting inside the vault is a real exposure if the vault syncs anywhere; the companion engine is a separate binary install from release downloads; hourly auto-sync of the index; 12 commits and 1 star.
didnt: Corroboration: local multimodal indexing corroborates our OCR/multimodal direction (our own OCR queue exists), and its disclosure completeness is the habit worth copying; the engine is not adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Mermaid Relay
type: Obsidian plugin (visual Mermaid editing over Markdown)
good: Refusing to round-trip what it cannot represent losslessly is the correct editor ethic; keeping layout out of the file keeps diagrams diffable and agent-editable; THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES ships at root.
bad: Valid drafts auto-save with no review step (acceptable for diagrams, recorded); 8 commits and 2 stars; the suggested companion set includes Claudian, which our owner has rejected — the suggestion is the plugin's content, noted not followed.
didnt: Corroboration: text-as-truth with read-only degradation instead of lossy conversion corroborates our portable-source discipline; nothing is adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Azure Wiki Preview
type: Obsidian plugin (Azure DevOps Wiki dialect preview)
good: Fidelity to how the page will actually publish, with zero source mutation, is the right shape for dialect preview; failure is surfaced inline (unterminated blocks) rather than swallowed; limits are stated as a section, not discovered.
bad: Six commits and 0 stars; the preview fixes the view, not the index — tags/search/graph still see the dialect as broken, by the README's own admission; it serves Azure Wiki clones specifically, while our wiki's reader surface is the Lens portal, not Obsidian.
didnt: Corroboration: previewing the target dialect faithfully without mutating source corroborates our verify-against-the-live-target standard; nothing is adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Cove
good: The mass-failure sanity guard is a small rule that prevents a whole class of false conclusions; status restoration on recovery (not just flag-clearing) respects prior state; files-as-truth with a derived index is the portable shape; interchange format support is real, not promised.
bad: Health checks can also run periodically in the background — scheduled network chatter against every saved origin; adding a bookmark fetches the page's metadata from its origin by default; 21 commits and 3 stars.
didnt: Corroboration: the all-checks-fail-means-the-checker-failed guard corroborates our failure-accounting rules (a failed source is reported as failed, not as finding nothing); the bookmark surface is not adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Valeon
type: Obsidian plugin (publishing/sync for the Valeon platform)
good: Validation gates the irreversible act rather than following it; reconcile's report-first flow is the correct order for identity-writing operations; the local-state block never leaks into the published artefact because only a transport copy is rewritten.
bad: On publish, posts with fewer than 5 tags are topped up automatically in the background to 5–15 tags — silent metadata mutation at the moment of publication, disclosed in the README but automatic; the API token is pasted into a settings field with custody unspecified; the plugin is useless without the invite-only Valeon platform (single-vendor dependence).
didnt: Corroboration: lint-gates-publish, preview-then-apply reconcile and transport-copy rewriting corroborate our publish discipline; the platform itself is not adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: R2DO Sync
type: Obsidian plugin + Cloudflare Workers (self-hosted E2E vault sync, optional MCP)
good: The deny-required deploy gate is the strongest authorisation shape in this wave — access narrowing as a forced decision, not an option; sync and agent credentials are separated so the always-on half never holds the key; trade-offs are priced honestly in the README, including what the encrypted claim does not cover.
bad: AGPL-3.0 puts the code in the ideas-only class under our licence discipline; agent write/delete tools ask for no confirmation — snapshot retention is the only net; the agent Worker concentrates the vault master key in a cloud worker by design; the sync surface (Workers, R2, Durable Objects, QR device joining) is a lot of machinery to trust at 143 commits and 1 star.
didnt: Rejected (licence: AGPL-3.0 — ideas only, no code taken): the deny-list-as-deploy-gate and the separate, separately-revocable agent credential are credited in-row as corroborating our door design from the sync side. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Pumice
type: Obsidian plugin + self-hosted Python sync server
good: Merge is attempted before any winner-takes-all rule; the two most dangerous sync options carry their threat models in the settings table itself; recovery is a designed surface (history, snapshots, file recovery), not a support request; per-file publish consent via frontmatter.
bad: End-to-end encryption is optional and off by default; vault identity is the folder name, and a mismatch 'isn't rejected, it just syncs as an unrelated vault' — disclosed, but a silent-split footgun; live multi-device sync is the multi-writer direction our single-writer-plus-git design declines; 148 commits and 0 stars.
didnt: Corroboration: merge-first conflicts and reasoned defaults-off for trust-boundary syncs corroborate sync-design judgement; the live multi-writer model is not our route, so nothing is adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: PKV Sync
type: Obsidian plugin + self-hosted server (Git-backed sync, release mirror)
good: Git as the truth layer gives real history and rollback rather than a sync vendor's opaque state; conflicts become files you resolve, not silent choices; the admin-can-read limit is disclosed instead of implied away by 'self-hosted'.
bad: AGPL-3.0 puts the code in the ideas-only class under our licence discipline; the built-in MCP's write posture ('maintain your notes') shows no approval gating in the mirror's documentation; multi-user/multi-vault means operating a server, with content readable by its admin by design.
didnt: Rejected (licence: AGPL-3.0 — ideas only, no code taken): git-as-source-of-truth and visible conflict files are credited in-row. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Safe Vault
type: Obsidian plugin (archive backup with age encryption + git)
good: Tool composition beats hand-rolled crypto; age-by-default is the right default cipher choice; the placement/exclusion rules show the author thought about how backups fail, not just how they succeed.
bad: Delete-then-create as the default collision strategy means a failed archive creation after the delete leaves no backup at all — the riskiest default in this batch; exact-match-only exclusions are brittle (one renamed folder silently re-includes a subtree); 41 commits and 0 stars.
didnt: Corroboration: age-encrypted archive backups composed from audited system tools corroborate our backup posture (our nightly wiki zip and parts route are our own); the destructive default is recorded against the design, and nothing is adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Secure Git Sync
type: Obsidian plugin (password-confirmed encrypted Git sync + LAN sync)
good: The crypto design is genuinely careful — path-bound authenticated encryption prevents object-swapping, and encrypted-by-default beats opt-in; deletion non-propagation on LAN sync is the safe asymmetry; respecting the user's existing remote configuration instead of recreating it shows workflow manners.
bad: Making post-sync verification optional trades away assurance exactly where an encrypted pipeline needs it; LAN transfer is plaintext by default; 13 commits and 2 stars is thin provenance for a cryptography product; selected Obsidian configuration still syncs as plaintext in encrypted mode.
didnt: Corroboration: encrypted-remote-over-plaintext-local with password-gated pushes corroborates our custody split (readable at home, protected at rest remotely); nothing is adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Halyard Sync
type: Obsidian plugin (git sync via libgit2-WASM, mobile included)
good: Conflicts are escalated to a reviewable branch with a real diff UI instead of being resolved inside someone's notes; failure at every step degrades to 'parked and reported', never to loss; key-missing is a named, blocking, all-or-nothing state — partial encrypted sync is refused by design.
bad: A WASM git engine at 30 commits is an ambitious trust ask; OAuth device flow appears only where distribution client IDs are configured, so sign-in quality varies by build; requested PAT scopes are broad (GitLab's api scope creates merge requests vault-wide); the managed-policy machinery (.gitignore marked blocks, byte snapshot/restore) is intricate.
didnt: Corroboration: the conflict-branch-instead-of-markers model and all-or-nothing key gating corroborate our never-lose-work sync ethics strongly; our wiki syncs with plain git from the shell, so nothing is adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Publish on GitHub
type: Obsidian plugin (selective publishing to GitHub Pages/Jekyll)
licence: No licence (checked: no LICENSE file at root, no licence statement in README, GitHub API license field null)
good: Selection by explicit tag is the correct publish boundary — publication is opt-in per note; scanning outbound links for private targets is the leak check selective publishers need and most skip; section-level redaction respects that a note can be partly public.
bad: No licence means all rights reserved by default — ideas only; the private-link notice is non-blocking, so the leak check warns but still lets a publish proceed; Reset Repo is a destructive recovery presented casually ('safely'); a data.json sits in the repository root; the README's 'premium' framing oversells a 17-commit plugin.
didnt: Rejected (no licence — ideas only, no code taken): tag-gated selection plus private-target link scanning is credited in-row as corroborating our public-edition extraction discipline. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: ATProto Sync
type: Obsidian plugin + CLI (E2E-encrypted sync to ATProto PDS)
good: Encryption is the default and covers metadata (filenames/titles), not just bodies; the public/private boundary is per-note and reversible with key rotation; permissions are itemised by capability rather than gestured at.
bad: A public toggle on a federated protocol makes a note world-readable, and the README does not address copies that may already have replicated when it is toggled back — re-encryption protects the record, not the network's memory; the 5 MB reference-PDS blob limit caps attachments; app-password sign-in is the weaker auth route and is supported alongside OAuth.
didnt: Corroboration: per-note publish with fresh-key re-encryption and conflict preservation corroborate our selective-publication and never-lose-work rules; the ATProto substrate is not adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Cloud WebDAV Sync
good: Planning-only by default is the correct shipped posture for a sync engine that can overwrite; capability probing before choosing a concurrency strategy respects weak servers instead of corrupting against them; every ambiguous state has a named, human-gated exit rather than a timeout-and-hope.
bad: The machinery is enormous for WebDAV, a substrate whose capability variance is the entire problem — the design spends most of its complexity distrusting its own transport; experimental at 26 commits with broader server/mobile coverage admittedly unvalidated; force-recovery actions bypass the very protections the design builds (gated by confirmation, but present).
didnt: Corroboration: the strongest corroboration in this batch for our write-safety rules — no blind replay, read-back reconciliation, corruption reported not repaired; the WebDAV substrate itself is not adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Clippings Dedupe
good: The merge precedence is the right one — human writing beats machine duplication, and conflicting human comments are both kept rather than adjudicated; untouched-when-clean limits blast radius; backup-before-rewrite is observed even for a small utility.
bad: Merging runs automatically — 2 seconds after a clip lands, and a full sweep on startup — with no per-run review; identity-by-exact-text breaks silently if the clipper's formatting drifts; backups live inside the plugin's own folder, the durability caveat seen across this wave; 17 commits and 0 stars.
didnt: Corroboration: comment-preserving dedupe corroborates our merge ethics (the human annotation layer outranks duplicated machine content); the plugin is not adopted. (completion pass, 2026-10-21)

name: Block Reference Enhancer
good: Dangling references are a designed review workflow, not an error string; source preservation is a stated rule (older forms supported, never gratuitously rewritten); reference counts and jump-to-source make block citations navigable in both directions.
